body:
With a population of 494,228, Morris County is the 10th-most populous county in New Jersey. In 2017, Morris County had the second lowest crime rate in the state1. Its crime rate dropped to a 20-year low; even though the population had increased by nearly 20% from the 1990s. “Experts attribute the drop to a number of factors, including better training of police officers, more cooperation among agencies and advancing technology.”2

Searching for a Total Solution

In 2011, the Morris County Department of Law and Public Safety began to explore the implementation of a countywide records management system (RMS) to provide situational awareness to the officers in the County.

CSI Technology Group was contracted to provide the total solution.

Within the first five years, 27 individual police departments, along with the Morris County Sheriff’s Office and Morris County Park Police, had migrated to CSI’s total, countywide solution.

Crime data analysis is a difficult task when you are not sharing real-time RMS data. CSI and InfoShare® have made this possible. The accessibility to real-time data has helped our detectives piece together cases that probably would never have been solved. Our agency recently has also assisted a neighboring Union County city with a robbery case. A phone call and a simple inquiry, returned data in the InfoShare® System from another Township which immediately identified the suspect. An arrest was made an hour later. Whether it is the ability to share contact information, review images from other jurisdictions cases or review other agencies reports the InfoShare® system is an invaluable tool. It is amazing all the benefits the system has provided to date.

Lt. Joseph Longo
Madison Police Department

Previous Challenges

Prior to contracting with CSI, each of these agencies had independent record management systems provided by different vendors. There was no sharing of information; agencies could not view or gather information from each other. Each agency was then required to pay those vendors for annual maintenance, licensing, and support. In addition, many of these other vendors would periodically “update” their software and in turn, require the agency to “re-purchase” the upgrade at great expense.

The Solution

By migrating to the countywide system, the individual municipalities united behind one shared system, realizing large cost savings as they did not have to maintain those incumbent systems. CSI supported these agencies’ migration to the RMS by transferring their diverse data into the countywide database, including cases from as far back as 1954. Now, all these files are included in the Morris County RMS. Unlike other vendors, CSI’s data conversions consist of a complete integration of the data from the prior systems tables and fields into the RMS tables and fields. The data is not located in a separate database but saved in the RMS format. The cases are handled in exactly the same manner as if the case was originally entered into RMS.

The RMS interfaces with the Morris County Department of Law and Public Safety CAD System, which provides all of the information to the RMS interface. Any transactions or searches performed in the CAD system are routed over to the RMS completely. Any and all vehicle and person lookups and searches are inserted into the cases which they pertain to.

CSI InfoShare® RMS

CSI presents a total solution, a complete record/case management tool with data sharing capabilities and fully integrated modules for investigation and evidence processing. The RMS revolutionizes police data collection and reporting, providing a comprehensive solution for capturing data and tracking cases, from the moment a Call for Service (CFS) is received to case disposition.

We’ve been using the Morris RMS since 2013. The InfoShare® RMS has greatly expanded our information sharing capability throughout Morris County. Officers can quickly and efficiently import Driver’s License and Vehicle Registration Data to reports by querying the NJMVC Interface. It is also a great investigative tool for our officers because they can query a suspect's name to find out previous addresses, phone numbers, and any prior dealings with law enforcement in Morris County.

Chief Thomas Wiliver
Chester Police Department
CSI’s RMS and CAD products successfully provide complete integration with many other vendors’ CAD and RMS products. The RMS is also designed to support inter-agency data sharing and can support the operations of various law enforcement and prosecutorial agencies in the county. Clients in New Jersey can electronically submit files and records to county prosecutors, who support the case management of their respective county agencies, beginning with the Morris County Department of Law and Public Safety.

InfoShare® RMS provides a Total Integration Solution to Public Safety Agencies

RMS offers unique features and specialized tools that can be easily extended through the integration of third-party analysis tools. CSI provides an RMS that is accessible by all authorized users to create a single knowledgebase, within and between sectors and precincts, and that facilitates the sharing of resources within the agency. Agencies also have control over user groups, support files, form template generators permissions, and other settings so that the agency’s administrators are empowered to maintain the system as requirements demand.

While we pride ourselves on unparalleled customer service and support, we also know that the convenience of “getting it done immediately” is the right thing to do for our clients.

CSI InfoShare® RMS includes:

  • Interface to the Morris County Prosecutor’s Office (send to prosecutor)
  • Interface with the Morris County Correctional Facility (send to corrections)
  • Evidence module
  • UCR and NIBRS reporting
  • Fleet management
  • Permits and licensing
  • Expungements
  • Redaction and Bates stamping
  • NJMVC and NCIC interface
  • Total information sharing between all participating police departments
  • Crime Mapping
  • Crime Analysis
When utilizing the InfoShare® RMS, participating departments can search across municipal boundaries. The RMS application has two embedded, powerful analysis tools: Crime Mapping and Link Analysis, providing the ability to find patterns of criminal activity through more accurate filtering. Furthermore, data in the RMS can be exported to third-party, specialized analysis products, extending the data analysis ability.

Crime Analysis Tool

The ability to search an individual’s name for all police contacts including those that do not end in an arrest. This is especially important when conducting background investigations of any kind i.e. personnel and firearms applications. In the past this information was only identified by calling another agency.

Through InfoShare® you can obtain reports and related discovery during an active investigation that can be immediately downloaded, negating the need to call the other (participating) agency and saving valuable time.

Charlie Brady (Retired)
Morris County Prosecutor's Offices
The major advantages of CSI InfoShare® RMS are:
  • Off-the-shelf system yet highly configurable (support file and business rule-driven).
  • Complete application that supports all aspects of a case from start to finish, from investigation to arrest, with historical information analysis to prevent future crime activity and/or to support the next investigation.
  • A “PUSH-TO-INTEL” function to transmit reports for evaluation by the Intel unit for 28CFR23 Criminal Intelligence.
  • Provides real-time data and resource sharing between multiple law enforcement agencies with single-point data entry and permission- or role-based security access control.

  • Tracking assignments and responsibilities through User Inboxes allow users to easily identify cases that they are assigned to without searching.
  • The data conversion service accurately converts legacy data (including documents and multimedia files) to the InfoShare® RMS database. Converted records and files are integrated into the database and accessible through the RMS, not as note fields or fields accessed through an interface to the legacy data.
  • Global search capability provides access to data across jurisdictional borders, enabling information sharing citywide (or further).

CSI’s Track Record

The RMS, together with other applications, is robustly designed yet flexible enough to facilitate upgrades to meet the needs of a rapidly changing environment. For over 30 years, our systems have evolved significantly, based on our focused effort to provide our clients with superior information technology.

In the years since Morris County RMS went live, InfoShare® RMS has expanded to over 150 clients—several standalone police agencies, New Jersey counties, and states—participating in a number of countywide or regional RMS applications, which provide the agencies a lower cost of ownership and increases situational awareness as to the events taking place in the surrounding jurisdictions.

title: Camden County Regional Records Management System, Powered by CSI InfoShare<sup>®</sup>, Grows to 29 Agencies
shareTitle: Camden County Regional Records Management System, Powered by CSI InfoShare®, Grows to 29 Agencies
body:
CSI Technology Group is excited to announce that the police departments of Pennsauken and Berlin Borough have joined the Camden County InfoShare® Regional Records Management System (RMS).

Background

Camden County is located in the southwest portion of New Jersey. It is connected to Philadelphia by three major Delaware River bridge crossings. As of the 2019 U.S. Census estimate, the county's population was 506,471, making it the state's eighth-largest county.

Challenge Accepted

Between late 2012 and early 2013, the Camden County Chiefs of Police Association launched an effort to find a RMS vendor to power a shared services agreement between six agencies. Bellmawr Police Chief William Walsh led this effort, as the Bellmawr Police Department has been a driving force for technology and shared services among Camden County law enforcement for well over two decades.

After exploring several RMS vendors and conducting their due diligence, they decided to partner with CSI Technology Group and power their Regional RMS with the InfoShare® RMS platform including evidence, personnel suite, eTicketing, and RMS-MDT.

The Camden County Chiefs of Police Association Shared RMS Project went live on Oct. 3, 2013 in six departments. Since that date, 23 additional agencies have voluntarily joined the project, totaling approximately 1,000 officers, as well as support staff. There are a number of factors that make this project very special:
  • All of the agencies had their data converted from their prior vendors, enabling officers from different parts in the county to access millions of records.
  • This project is hosted by the Bellmawr Police Department, and the Camden County Chiefs of Police Association is the organization that oversees it.
  • This is not a county-led initiative. These agencies volunteered to join the Camden County Regional Police RMS because they understood the numerous benefits of data sharing.
  • This is a true shared service with real cost savings and tangible results.

Covid-19 Impact

Most recently, the Pennsauken and Berlin Borough police departments have joined the regional RMS. CSI’s deepest admiration and respect go out to both agencies, as they undertook this transition at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. The CSI staff worked closely and tirelessly with both agencies to develop and implement virtual training and around-the-clock, go-live support of the application to ensure quality hands-on user training and a smooth rollout.

Members of Pennsauken PD training in CSI Technology virtual classroom

Regional RMS at a Glance

A regional RMS is a county or statewide system that provides for the entry, storage, retrieval, retention, sharing, viewing, and archiving of information, records, and documents or files, spanning a breadth of various size law enforcement agencies and operations.

Intelligence and information sharing in law enforcement largely depends on the availability of accurate real-time and historical data. It is no secret that criminal activity knows no geographical boundary lines. Other benefits include:
  • Significant cost savings from a stand-alone system
  • Data sharing between agencies that can reduce crime and quality-of-life issues
  • Find the right information and find it quickly
  • Perform full or partial searches on a countywide level
  • Identify crime trends and patterns, as well as associations between suspects
  • Collaborate with other agencies
  • Comprehensive data sharing can improve investigations, recover stolen property, locate fugitives, and increase arrests
  • Information sharing is greatly improved across all partner regional RMS agencies
  • Each agency can control its own data and information
  • Data sharing inherently leads to interagency collaboration and problem solving

Regional Data Sharing Results in Case Success

There are thousands of police agencies in the United States, many of which do a subpar job of information sharing. However, many police departments realize that they can more effectively serve their communities and solve more crimes using data collected not only by their agency but also by numerous other agencies.

Real-time availability of information is of paramount importance. Supervisors, detectives, and officers on the street need real-time information to deploy personnel, supply leads to investigative staff, connect associates, conduct full or partial searches of many variations, and identify crime trends and quality-of-life issues.

Such is the case with the Camden County RMS. As a result of implementation, many Camden County agencies have improved the way they input, gather, manage, search for, and share information with other partner agencies.

Case Solved: Robbery/Shooting

In October 2019, officers from a Camden County municipality were dispatched to a call of a 21-year-old male who was bleeding. The specific nature of the injury was unknown at the time, but it was reported that the victim had a hole in his leg.

As officers approached the scene, it became immediately apparent that the injury was a gunshot wound. Officers asked the victim where the incident occurred, and his response was vague; he stated "back there" as he pointed to a wooded area.

The victim was otherwise uncooperative and refused to provide a more specific location. He was also unable to identify who had shot him. He provided several general details, relaying that he had been walking through the woods when two unknown males passed by, and that he then heard a loud noise and felt something in his leg. He went on to say that he initially did not realize he had been shot.

Members of other law enforcement agencies arrived to assist, and K-9 units were deployed in an attempt to find the shooting scene and/or suspects.

While on scene, investigators observed two sets of fresh bicycle wheel impressions left in the soft sand. They also observed footprint impressions that matched the soles of the sneakers worn by the shooting victim.

The search provided investigators with valuable information, as well as locations to pursue in furtherance of the investigation, which featured numerous surveillance cameras.

Recovered surveillance footage revealed two suspects on what appeared to be mountain bikes, as well as one person seen on foot. There was also another person walking in a different direction. Suddenly, the two individuals on foot started running, almost simultaneously. Another nearby surveillance camera captured the entire shooting incident.

During a careful review of the footage, it appeared that the shooting victim had actually shot himself while running from a female he had met with briefly. That female had arrived at the scene in a vehicle, accompanied by others.

The video of the shooting also showed the female and two other males running toward her after the shooting. Images of these three individuals were also captured on video footage from other nearby cameras. The vehicle that the female and others arrived in was also very distinguishable, but a license plate was not captured.

Still photos of the vehicle and individuals were shown to patrol units for identification. One officer immediately recognized the vehicle, the female, and another male from previous police encounters.

The officer searched his case history through the Camden regional RMS system, revealing the license plate for the vehicle. Further review of the RMS case history of the registered owner of the vehicle in question revealed associates who were connected to the owner of the vehicle. Driver’s license photos for the vehicle owner and associates were obtained, and these photos appeared to match some of the people who were caught on video surveillance footage at the scene.

Investigators met with one of the persons identified through the vehicle owner’s RMS case history and conducted an interview. The case turned out to be a botched drug deal, in which a would-be robber accidentally shot himself in the leg.

In furtherance of the investigation, the suspect was re-interviewed but initially stuck to his original story of being shot by unknown actor(s). That only lasted until investigators confronted him with surveillance footage. At this point, the suspect made an admission of the intended robbery–and the fact that he had shot himself.

As a result of the investigation, the suspect was lodged into the county jail, charged with numerous offenses.

Case Solved: Vehicle Battery Theft

A Camden County chain-store theft case involved a perpetrator who had stolen an entire pallet of car batteries. Detectives investigating the case initially had little to go on. Fortunately, surveillance video captured the theft, along with the suspect’s clothing and what appeared to be a red Jeep. The only identifying characteristics available for the vehicle were three digits of a temporary license plate that was on the vehicle.

Utilizing the Camden Regional RMS, detectives conducted a search for a red Jeep with the three digits of the partial temporary plate. This search yielded a car stop one hour before the theft at the chain store.

The stop was in a neighboring jurisdiction that is a regional RMS partner agency. Detectives contacted that agency and obtained body camera footage of the car stop.

At this point, it became immediately apparent that it was the same perpetrator seen on the chain store surveillance video, wearing the same clothes. After further investigation, the subject was charged with the substantial theft and lodged in the county jail.

Further investigation by the detectives found hundreds of vehicle batteries that were stockpiled at a property under the defendant’s control. The stockpile of batteries had been stolen from multiple jurisdictions in Camden and surrounding counties.

In Closing

We at CSI would like to express our sincere appreciation to the Camden County Chiefs of Police Association and the growing number of agencies for making Camden Regional RMS such a success.

Thank you for a favorable and fruitful partnership lasting nearly seven years! We look forward to future growth and many more innovative years of the Camden Regional RMS.

title: Cape May County Continues to Grow its Regional CAD/RMS Project
shareTitle: Cape May County Continues to Grow its Regional CAD/RMS Project
body:
CSI Technology Group is proud to announce that the Cape May County Office of Emergency Management (CMCOEM) Regional CAD/RMS Project continues to grow. Working in conjunction with CMCOEM, CSI continues to provide the Regional Police and Fire CAD and RMS with a centralized command and control system which allows first responders to focus on critical incidents. The Regional CAD/RMS also permits all the regional agencies to analyze calls for service and complete crime/incident analysis.

Background

Cape May County is the southernmost county in New Jersey with over 97,000 residents. Cape May County is a consistent summer destination with 30-miles of beaches, attracting vacationers from all over the country. During the summer, the population grows to over 750,000. The CMCOEM Regional CAD/RMS Project started in 2016 with seven CAD Centers dispatched for Lower Township Police Department and the Cape May County Sheriff’s Department. The Regional Project then added all three of Lower Township Fire Departments, the Lower Township Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Stone Fire Department/EMS, and Avalon Fire Department/EMS. This regional project started with a partnership among CMCOEM, municipal leaders, and County Freeholders.

CSI has been with us from the beginning, and we could not have asked for a better partner.

Director Martin Pagliughi
Cape May County Office of Emergency Management
In May 2019, the Wildwood Crest Police Department, Wildwood Crest Fire Department, and the Wildwood Crest EMS joined the CMCOEM Regional Project. In December 2019, the Stone Harbor Police Department joined, and the Avalon Police Department is scheduled to join in September 2020. Future growth, beyond 2020, is ongoing as several other first responder agencies are in discussions with CMCOEM.

The $5 Million Challenge

Getting agencies to buy into a $5-million, multi-year consolidated dispatch center with local acceptance and participation by the municipalities was going to be difficult. In spite of this, CMCOEM tackled this challenge head on. Definitive and accurate communications are critical in public safety. Plus, making sure the right police, fire, or emergency medical services are promptly notified is crucial.

According to Director Martin Pagliughi of CMCOEM, “When we were planning the regional communication center, we looked at numerous CAD/RMS software companies. We decided on the InfoShare® system from CSI Technology Group. CSI has been with us from the beginning, and we could have not asked for a better partner. As we moved into our new communications center and added new departments, CSI has worked with us to ensure these transitions worked seamlessly. They did not just hand us a system and say, it is all yours.”

Each agency faced different challenges before joining the Regional Project: no data sharing outside of their agency, limited configurability to the application without a significant cost or wait, search functions were limited, and less user-friendly interfaces.

The Solution

CMCOEM Regional agencies now enjoy a robust Master Name, Master Vehicle, and Master Location, Index. These allow officers to search for specific information about cases, associated persons, vehicles, or flags assigned to a location. The Regional design allows all agencies on the platform to access and share this information with each other automatically. CSI worked with each agency in successfully converting and migrating all the previous case data.

InfoShare® CAD Center provides real-time computer-aided dispatch (CAD) that is fluid, dynamic, and flows seamlessly from call creation through completion. The CAD provides immediate access to critical information for the CAD Operator and MDT users in the responding units, keeping all staff and officers informed. To that end, the Regional CAD Center is viewed as the “brain” that communicates and coordinates all the public safety resources that are required to handle the problem in the quickest time.

Cape May County Office of Emergency Management CAD Center

CSI Technology – The Patented InfoShare® Product

title: Victim/Witness Services in the Covid-19 Era
shareTitle: Victim/Witness Services in the Covid-19 Era
body:
When the State of New Jersey was forced to close its government institutions, one group of citizens that were severely impacted was the victims of crime. Victim Witness Coordinators and Advocates still needed to provide support services and information to these victims, who have the right to be kept informed. In many instances, the only source of comfort for some victims comes from the Coordinators and Advocates at the County Prosecutor’s Offices. The New Jersey Constitution contains the Crime Victim’s Bill of Rights, among those rights is “to have inconvenience associated with participation in the criminal justice minimized to the fullest extent possible.”

The InfoShare® Victim Witness Suite aided New Jersey counties in fulfilling their constitutional obligations despite the pandemic and the “new normal” that everyone was facing. As expressed by one of our client agencies, “The Victim Witness tools and modules that your team has developed over the years have been a vital lifeline throughout our time of telecommuting. As many of us were thrust into this “new normal” of “working from home” there was one that we all felt confident in and that was the support of CSI. While we were trying to grasp the fact of our new reality, you reached out and immediately offered your support and services.”

Victim/Witness Notification Service

The InfoShare® Vitim Witness Suite is intertwined with the eScreening/Central Judicial Process and Prosecution of criminal cases, which are also contained in the InfoShare® product line, and contains the following elements:
  • Victim/Witness Biographical Data: Within each case is the pedigree information for victims including their contact information and relationship to the case (victim, victim-survivor, victim-parent, etc.)

  • Letter Generators: Based on case event data that is entered and/or imported from a variety of interfaces, a wide array of notification letters are electronically generated that can be printed & mailed, e-mailed, or sent to the Victim/Witness Public Facing Portal.

  • Victim/Witness Public Facing Portal: This portal allows victims to register an account, track their case through the Justice System, send the Victim Impact Statement, have input on plea bargains, and other related matters. The victim can also pose questions and find a plethora of resources with links geared specifically for their type of victimization.

  • Victim Stat Tracker: While the Coordinators and Advocates are performing their services, they can easily enter their activity so that administrative and grant reports can be generated with ease. Thus, allowing the dedicated Victim Witness Coordinators and Advocates more time providing important services and less time doing paperwork.

  • Victim/Witness Smart Phone App with Mapping: This application has all of the features of the Public Facing Portal with the convenience of being on the victims’ phones and also includes an optional mapping feature that will provide door-to-door instructions to victims to get to the services they may need such as a shelter, hospital, or other social services.

Victim/Witness Smartphone App with Mapping Feature

During the COVID-19 Pandemic, the New Jersey Victim/Witness Coordinators were able to leverage the InfoShare® Victim/Witness Suite to maximize their efforts while working remotely from home:
  • Coordinators and Advocates have had the basic but essential ability to access victim contact information, enabled by InfoShare®’s patented Engine®, which accommodates distance working via VPN and/or other CJIS compliant channels. Without having remote access to this lifeline would result in no contact with the victims for months, leaving them feeling even more confused and abandoned.

  • Because InfoShare® products are designed to complement one another and streamline operations, the notes and general victim services notes feature allowed Coordinators and Advocates to see what communications had already taken place in the case or with a victim. This capability was crucial at a time when the staff did not have the same access to their prosecutorial colleagues that they did while physically in the office.

  • The Victim/Witness Public Facing Portal and Phone Apps allowed Coordinators and Advocates to offer portal registration or email notification of letters. As one of our other client agencies pointed out, “We were physically out of our office for over two months with no ability to print out the Victim Witness letters like we used to do on a daily basis. As a result of the Letter Generator, the Portal, and the Phone App, we effectively e-mailed and posted everyone’s letters.”

  • Coordinators and Advocates had access to all relevant case materials such as investigative reports, allowing the staff to assist and support claims for crime compensation with the Victims of Crime Compensation Office.

  • Coordinators and Advocates could aid victims and witnesses by accessing case notes and reports, enabling Prosecutor’s Offices to continue to sign many U visa certifications as appropriate. This invaluable public service helps undocumented immigrants, who have been the victims of crime. Without this service, immigrants would often not come forward, and criminals would continue to prey upon those communities.
CSI Technology Group is very proud of the InfoShare® Victim Witness Suite, an invaluable service that would benefit any agency in the United States that cares about its victims. Oftentimes, the criminal justice system is confusing and intimidating. However, by putting victims in contact with dedicated Victim/Witness Coordinators and Advocates, we are making a difference in the experience. Being a victim is a traumatic event, no matter the crime, because the person’s own sense of safety and well-being are violated. Putting tools into victim’s hands empowers and guides them through the Criminal Justice System just a bit more easily.

title: Montgomery County Successfully Deploys a Countywide Law Enforcement Solution
shareTitle: Montgomery County Successfully Deploys a Countywide Law Enforcement Solution
body:
“It won’t work.” “It’s bound to fail.” “There has never been a successful installation of a countywide system in Pennsylvania.” That was the impression of others outside of Montgomery County in 2016 when it was announced that CSI Technology Group was awarded the contract to implement a countywide law enforcement solution.

Montgomery County sits in the Southeastern corner of the Pennsylvania. With a population of 830,000, it is the third most populous county, after Philadelphia and Allegheny Counties.

In 2016, the Department of Public Safety, along with other county stakeholders, sought a countywide law enforcement RMS solution that would enable data sharing between local agencies, County Detectives, the Sheriff’s and District Attorney’s Offices, and Prosecutors. The system needed to be scalable, easily supported, and centrally managed. And the solution needed to enhance the ability of law enforcement to navigate the criminal investigation process, reduce the time to resolution, and improve public safety.

County’s Objectives

The County’s objectives for a countywide solution were clear:
  • Improve the safety of police officers
  • Supply law enforcement with investigation tools to help direct them through the investigation process and reduce the time to resolution
  • Enhance efficiency and accuracy of data collection
  • Receive or forward RMS data electronically to external data sources
  • Enable centralized support for all locations to minimize the impact on users
  • Require a flexible software design that does not inhibit adding future features and integrations
  • Deliver required state and federal reporting through automated processes, with minimal manual intervention

…the design of the application made the transition from our previous RMS to InfoShare® RMS seamless and our personnel adapted quickly.

Chief Jackson
Lower Providence Township
Police Department

CSI InfoShare® RMS

The following key factors are what led Montgomery County to select CSI InfoShare®:

Support a true multi-tenant, multi-agency environment
InfoShare® RMS was built on a multi-agency, multi-tenant architecture design from the outset, allowing each police agency to retain its own identity, data, and operational differences. When officers log into the solution, they see their own logo, report formats, data, and so on. Yet the solution affords the benefit of shared resources. Searching for a person by name or vehicle by registration permits the officer to display all cases and reports containing that search criteria across all the agencies in the county.

Whereas other RMS vendors may charge for add-ons such as regional data sharing, CSI includes these system features at no cost. This is made possible by CSI’s forward thinking and smart software design.

… a great advantage in time saving during report writing, one entry (Persons and Vehicles) and it’s available to populate on any report for the case.

Detective Lukashunas
Rockledge Borough Police Department
An intuitive, feature-rich web-based user interface
Our modern, CJIS compliant, web-based technology is platform-independent accessible to law enforcement officers and other users. Any user with a device connected to the Internet has access to all RMS functions.

The customizable inbox format of the InfoShare® RMS home screen provides easy access to what officers and supervisors need during their tour, eliminating the need for users to search the system for assigned cases, tasks, or alerts. The report approval workflow process can also be customized to how a specific agency operates.

InfoShare® RMS Home Screen

Cloud Hosting with Amazon Web Services or Microsoft Azure for Government
Our flexible solutions can be implemented to meet each client’s preferences: hosted on premise or on the cloud, managed by CSI’s networking engineers or by the agency itself.

Having a cloud hosted solution provides numerous benefits and potential cost savings. Implementation time is much shorter since there is no waiting on server purchases or upgrades. Software updates are received immediately by all tenants in a multi-tenant environment. Disaster recovery is simplified. And damage to any physical structure due to a natural disaster or other event has no impact on the data. Cost savings come from not having to purchase and maintain server equipment, and not needing IT staff to maintain the equipment nor electricity to power it.

Migrate historical data from multiple disparate RMS systems
CSI has a team of engineers with specific expertise in legacy data conversions and migrations. We do not just copy our client’s data into a database but also cleanse and condense the data, merging duplicate instances of the same name or vehicle. If there is ever a need to reopen a legacy case, there is no need to log into another database as the data will be available in InfoShare®.

Because of our level of attention during the conversion process, the data will look and behave just like the case was entered into InfoShare® today. What this means is when running reports, users will be unable to distinguish between the old data and the new data.

Maximize the information gathered in the County’s Intergraph CAD system
CSI has vast experience in interfacing to most present-day CAD systems. A CAD interface capitalizes on information already entered by the dispatcher to improve accuracy and build the foundation of the case for the officer by eliminating the redundancy of having the user retype the same information, reducing the amount of user entry errors, and helping to streamline the report writing process.

The interface can provide a wealth of information to the RMS, which might be missed or omitted without this link, such as dispatcher’s notes, unit action times, GPS coordinates, closest intersection, building type, Area/Post, etc. This information may be vital at a later point in time or may provide information for reports that until this time were arduous or impossible to create.

As nice as a CAD interface to RMS is, a true CAD/RMS integration allows for more efficient operations and the ability to deploy new capabilities. Like our other offerings, InfoShare® CAD seamlessly integrates with InfoShare® RMS.

Interface with other critical systems in use throughout the county
At CSI we have several engineers whose job is specifically geared towards the design of interfaces with other vendor’s software. Montgomery County presented a list of required interfaces which have all been implemented. This quick implementation was achieved because of the well-thought-out infrastructure of InfoShare® solutions.

CSI has applied and was granted a patent titled "Application Developing Method and System". The patented product is a low-code development platform that allows for rapid application delivery with quick setup and enables our engineers to design flexible application customized to fulfill each agency’s unique requirements. In the long run, our proprietary technology significantly lowers training, deployment, modification, and maintenance costs.

The County’s list of other critical interfaces:

CLEAN – The Commonwealth Law Enforcement Assistance Network is utilized by the RMS to access driver license and motor vehicle information. Modifications were done to the Party and Vehicle Entry forms in InfoShare® RMS to allow the look-up and importing of information from CLEAN, which improves the accuracy of the data and reduces the time it takes to enter case information.

LEJIS – Law Enforcement Justice Information System is a Pennsylvania statewide information sharing initiative. This interface allows agencies to contribute case information to the program and provides an additional investigation tool for police officers.

ALPR Search – Automated License Plate Reader Search is an investigation tool incorporated into InfoShare® RMS. From the navigation panel of the RMS, a simple entry of a vehicle registration, a click of a button, and a search is performed of a regional database, returning hits in a matter of seconds. Images of the license plate are displayed along with the location, date, and time they were captured. A map is also displayed with pins for visual reference of the captured plates.

Crash Reporting System – An interface to Pennsylvania’s Crash Reporting System (PennDot) that capitalizes on the CAD and CLEAN interfaces to improve efficiency and reduce data entry errors. The interface validates entries to PennDot’s specifications. Upon supervisor approval, the report is electronically sent to PennDot. Included in this interface is a crash diagram drawing tool.

LiveScan – Fingerprint capture terminals by DataWorks Plus. This interface provides InfoShare® RMS with booking information such as fingerprints, booking photos, etc. We have also developed interfaces for other clients with SagemMorpho and Crossmatch Technologies for booking.

AOPC – Administrative Office of the Pennsylvania Courts contains two critical interfaces:

Electronic filing of traffic citations. To streamline processes and reduce data entry errors, Montgomery County required the direct filing of traffic citations to the Courts. This feature reduces the amount of time for completing traffic citations on scene. Agencies have the option of scanning drivers’ licenses and registration or entering the information using the CLEAN interface, greatly reducing time and typing errors. Furthermore, AOPC provides the traffic statutes and fines for the interface, reducing the chance of errors. Once the ticket is issued, the citation is in the Court system available to the magistrates.

Importation of Court Case Events and scheduling information. With a couple of clicks, agencies can send Discovery information to the District Attorney’s Office. Utilizing CSI’s InfoShare® eProsecution solution, the District Attorney’s Office can accept the Discovery information and use the data to build a case.

Using the Court Case Events interface, the eProsecution solution receives updated information on Docket Sheets and current scheduling information about the case.

From the dashboard inbox, to report writing, to evidence documentation, a user-friendly RMS that automatically submits to LEJIS, which then submits to N-DEx.

Chief Medwid
Lower Salford Township
Police Department

The Results

Contract signing took place mid-December 2016. On-boarding of the agencies commenced with the Sheriff’s Office in March 2018. By October 2018, within 7 months, 32 agencies were live with InfoShare® RMS. These agencies had their legacy data migrated and available in the RMS by February 2019.

The County developed a 5-year plan to implement the InfoShare® solution. Presently, the District Attorney’s Office is being on-boarded with our eProsecution solution. Once completed, Montgomery County will successfully provide a seamless end-to-end solution that enables all agencies to share case information—starting with the call for service, to the investigation, to the arrest, and finally the conclusion of prosecution.

InfoShare® has facilitated the County’s effort to streamline its processes, equip officers with tools to help guide them through the investigation process, and reduce the time to resolution. The county not only improved public safety but also saved time and money throughout the multiple layers of law enforcement.

title: Bergen County: Building and Maintaining a CAD/RMS System for a Regional Dispatch Center

Bergen PSOC currently handles 911 calls for 23 towns, and calls and dispatch of Police, EMS, and Fire units for 17 agencies on the county and local level.

Bergen County is located in the northeastern corner of New Jersey. With a population of nearly one million residents, it is the most populous county in the state. Bergen ranks high in quality of life indicators and hosts an extensive 9,000-acre park system for cultural and recreational activities. The site of the PSOC today stands in Mahwah, NJ, on the grounds of the Bergen County Law & Public Safety Institute.

Bergen County Public Safety Operations Center

Police officers on the street can now search the database of participating InfoShare® agencies for the identities and case histories of the people they are dealing with. With real-time information sharing, responders are better informed and perform their duties more safely.

InfoShare® has given us a tremendous benefit in answering and responding to emergency calls and sharing information with one another.

Director of Communications Frank DelVecchio
Bergen County PSOC

The data is simultaneously housed at the PSOC and other backup sites in the county. And InfoShare® MDT allowed every police officer to receive data from each call and respond as needed. Later these functions were expanded for use by EMS providers and firefighters.

MDT interfaced with InfoShare® RMS

This technology has brought the fire service to a new level of efficiency. Data from calls gets imported directly to the Fire RMS, so that NFIRS and other reports are easily created and sent directly to the appropriate state agency.

The Demarest Fire Department is dispatched through the Bergen County dispatch center, and we are using the CAD system from CSI. title: NJBPU Demonstrates Deep Commitment to Public Integrity and Transparency
shareTitle: NJBPU Demonstrates Deep Commitment to Public Integrity and Transparency
body:
CSI Technology Group has assisted the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) in demonstrating in the most public way possible its deep commitment to public integrity and transparency. CSI, working at the behest of NJBPU, has brought online a Public Search and Comment module that creates unprecedented transparency and access for the public into the workings of the Board. We are very proud of this accomplishment considering the impediments and difficulties imposed by the current public health situation.

The public search page is accessed by going to the NJBPU main website www.bpu.state.nj.us and then going to Document Search and then clicking the green link called “Access Public Document Search Now.” The main public access search page is a multi-function search page that also displays a list of Key Topics on the Board agenda. Users can click the Docket number and see all related publicly accessible documentation under that docket or use the search features to drill down into the docket database to find what they are looking for.

Main Public Document Search Page

The commitment to public transparency brings with it increased obligations regarding document integrity and organization. As a result, a major part of the project was developing an internal workflow in the main InfoShare® case and records management system (RMS) that allowed NJBPU staff to review and recategorize all the documents related to the dockets that were being made public. This also enabled NJBPU staff to validate the accessibility of thousands of dockets and tens of thousands of related documents in the run up to turning on the public access search page. The process to make all historical documentation within the NJBPU available to the public is ongoing.

The project team consisting of CSI and NJBPU staff adopted the principle that good search pages must be simple and intuitive for the user. Users can either search by docket number or with keywords. Some users know the matter that they are interested in and can enter a party name or the name of a related company. At the same time, users who are interested in a topic can use keywords to bring back a list of dockets related to their topic of interest. In the case where users want access to a docket that has not been made public, a request form triggers a workflow within the main InfoShare® application for an administrative user to review the docket and prepare it for public access. Requestors then receive an email telling them the docket is available.

A key part of the project was enhancing the application to allow public users to file comments and documents related to docketed matters with the NJBPU. After users find the docket that they are interested in, the web page allows them to upload comments from a webform or in the form of documents. These uploaded items become immediately available to all public users of the module. NJBPU staff, of course, can modify misplaced or inappropriate entries. Moreover, users interested in a particular matter can also subscribe for email updates when major events are scheduled.

Having committed to allowing the public to upload comments and documents to InfoShare® RMS, the NJBPU decided it was only logical that more formal uploads of applications and related documents be accepted through similar means. For a number of years, CSI has supported a public user upload system referred to as the “Attorney Portal.” With this tool, the NJBPU has allowed vetted users access to its docketing system for the purpose of uploading documents since about 2016. The users of the Attorney Portal must establish a separate MyNewJersey account and then apply for access to the NJBPU InfoShare® application. All the upload and comment features developed for the public web page were also installed for the vetted users of the Portal. In addition, the feature set was expanded such that the NJBPU can now use the Portal to accept virtually any kind of application. Recently, the NJBPU used this to accept virtually all the 2021 Community Solar program applications.

CSI is grateful for the opportunity to work with the NJBPU on this project. The State of New Jersey has a long-standing commitment to government transparency as reflected by some of the strongest open public records law in the country. CSI looks forward to working with other government agency partners to fulfill this commitment.

title: Jersey City, NJ, Public Safety, Police, and Fire Departments Implement a Unified Total Solution
shareTitle: Jersey City, NJ, Public Safety, Police, and Fire Departments Implement a Unified Total Solution
body:
CSI Technology is proud to announce that the Jersey City, N.J. Public Safety Department is now part of the growing InfoShare® family. The Jersey City Public Safety Communications Center now enjoys a unified total solution for both police and fire Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) as well as a fully integrated Records Management System (RMS) for both the Police and Fire departments.

Background

Jersey City is part of the New York City metropolitan area and is the second-most populous city in the State of New Jersey. The U.S. Census Bureau calculated the city's population at 262,075 in 2019, ranking it as the 80th-most populous incorporated place in the nation.

Jersey City is bounded on the east by the Hudson River and Upper New York Bay, and on the west by the Hackensack River and Newark Bay. With 30.7 miles of waterfront and extensive rail infrastructure and connectivity, the city is an important transportation terminus and distribution and manufacturing center for the Port of New York and New Jersey. Jersey City also shares significant mass transit connections with Manhattan.

“Under the direction of Director James Shea, the Department of Public Safety comprises the Police Department (JCPD), the Fire Department (JCFD), the Office of Emergency Management and Homeland Security (OEM), Parking Enforcement, and Fire Prevention. Public Safety continues to be a top priority for the Fulop Administration and Director Shea,” the city’s public safety website reads. “The hiring of over 430 police officers since 2013 has helped lift the city’s department from historic lows, to nearly 975 officers, significantly boosting police presence in some of the most crime-ridden areas. As one of the state’s largest cities, public safety is paramount.”

Division Breakdown

The Jersey City Public Safety Communications Center has approximately 80 dedicated public safety telecommunicator professionals that staff the Communications Division Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP).

Jersey City Police Department is the second-largest municipal police agency in the State of New Jersey, consisting of the aforementioned nearly 975 sworn police officers and roughly 700 civilian personnel providing premier public safety to the community.

Jersey City Fire Department is the largest fire department in the State of New Jersey and comprises 650 uniformed members and 50 civilian employees who provide unparalleled fire safety and service to the community.

The Challenge

Prior to the implementation of CSI InfoShare® Total Solution, Jersey City Public Safety relied heavily on several different systems and vendors. Police and fire communications were handled by two different CAD systems, and the RMS was housed in three different systems overall.
  • Two CAD systems required duplicate call for service (CFS) entry by both police and fire
  • The network did not share flags, hazards, and previous CFS between two different CADs because of the two different RMS systems
  • No joint single call for service when both police and fire were simultaneously involved
  • No single cohesive Master Location database shared between both agencies
  • Historical RMS data was stored in two police RMS systems and one fire RMS system
Multiple systems from separate vendors and contracts resulted in poor operational cohesion.

The Solution

Jersey City now enjoys a single robust CAD/RMS platform that provides cross-functionality between dispatchers, police, and fire.

We converted over 15 years’ worth of CAD and RMS data from the previous police CAD and RMS systems and nearly 25 years of fire CAD and RMS data to the new InfoShare® Jersey City Total Public Safety Solution. Jersey City’s Communications, Police, and Fire departments now possess a true Master Indices database.

CSI offers the most comprehensive structured data conversion services on the market. Legacy data is converted to our native CAD/RMS format. However, the original data is not simply copied but also cleansed, condensed, and standardized so that public safety personnel will never need to spend time re-entering old data, accessing legacy systems, or removing duplicate entries. A unique person exists in the InfoShare® system as a single consolidated entry and not as separate records in disparate systems.

Project Scope

Jersey City Communications, Police, and Fire departments utilize the InfoShare® CAD and fully integrated RMS for all their reporting, analysis, evidence tracking, mapping, personnel scheduling, fleet management, and much more. The InfoShare® Total Solution provides seamless functionality for over 2,400 total municipal employees.

Our Products

Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD)

Jersey City’s InfoShare® CAD provides unparalleled, real-time computer-aided dispatch that is intuitive and easy to navigate. It provides immediate access to vital information simultaneously to both the CAD operator and the police and fire MDT users in the field, keeping all staff informed and personnel safe on the streets.

Features include:
  • Configurable presets for color and layout of screens, accommodating a four-monitor display
  • Connectivity to E-911 system, displaying incoming calls
  • CFS intake form is automatically populated with ANI/ALI Information
  • Dispatchers immediately receive related information automatically created from the RMS database including hazmat, medical alerts, warning flags, previous calls for service, and any other client-specific external data sources
  • Police functionality displays directed patrol information and engagements within a directed patrol, separate from regular calls for service
  • Fire functionality immediately builds a dynamic unit recommendation based on the type of incident, location of emergency, availability of apparatus, equipment capabilities, and mutual aid requests
  • Flexible fire event escalation: request additional units from a single unit to a full alarm-level increase

PD Dispatch Supervisor examines CAD during go-live


Jersey City Fire CAD stations

Words cannot express what I witnessed today. I had serious doubts that we would meet today’s guidelines due to all the obstacles that were placed in our way. Not only did you succeed, you did so almost effortlessly and seamlessly. Your staff is tremendous and a gift to work with. As I look back I’m still amazed at what we accomplished! All this is above and beyond the services you extended to the Jersey City Department of Public Safety!

Robert A. Baker, Sr., MBA, CFE, DRCC
Director, Public Safety Communications & Information Technology

Law Enforcement RMS

The InfoShare® Law Enforcement RMS brings real-time analytical reporting to support JCPD’s command staff in strategic planning, tactical deployment, and the direction of its officers to emergent situations.

Our crime mapping offers a robust platform to map, visualize, analyze, and graph crime and calls for service incident patterns. Our mapping feature also offers analytical capabilities with graph generation.

The exclusive Ad Hoc Search Engine delivers comprehensive statistics and reports without the need of running multiple reports in several different databases. The user simply enters the search criteria as needed. The information from the criteria entered can be parsed out in countless reports and formats.

During our comprehensive hands-on training and post-go-live support of Jersey City officers, they were very impressed with the integration of the CAD Center and MDT with the RMS. Officers and supervisors were particularly pleased with the amount of time saved when running parties in the CAD or MDT and having the party information automatically fed and readily available for them in the RMS. This feature not only saves time but also helps ensure accuracy by allowing officers to avoid having to re-type the same information repeatedly.

Some additional features include:
  • Regular and supplemental reports generated according to JCPD’s format and requirements
  • Complete RMS functionality within the MDT application
  • Configuration to the agency’s workflow
  • Total integration with other InfoShare® products and modules including eTicketing, CAD, Investigation, and Prosecutor
  • Police reports can be electronically submitted to the Prosecutor’s Office with all supporting documents
  • Embedded interface with LiveScan systems to automatically capture prints, palms, and photos at the time of booking, with storage directed to the case in the RMS

Fire RMS

Designed to fully meet NFIRS 2015 specifications, InfoShare® Fire RMS is a unique solution that encompasses all phases of fire department management and reporting from the initial reported incident to the validation and submission of the NFIRS report.

Our platform provides JCFD the ability to complete multiple after-action reports for various apparatuses, while ensuring consistent and accurate population of names and locations through Master Indices.

Through up-to-date building, premise, hazard, and hydrant data, the Fire RMS provides real-time information from the apparatus MDT or desktop, which raises awareness of potential dangers and threats that could compromise firefighter safety.

We also incorporate intuitive, enhanced search features and management reports that allow for easier statistical gathering when completing safety reports, grant applications, or submissions to various entities such as the Insurance Services Office (ISO).

The Jersey City Fire Department’s leadership has worked tirelessly, side by side with our staff, to ensure that our NFIRS-compliant InfoShare® Fire RMS and Fire CAD are both configured to support the mission of the Jersey City Fire Department.

The system is:
  • Designed to support JCFD’s report workflow and approval requirements
  • Inclusive of full event details stored in the Fire RMS, so that officers have all information readily available to complete their reports. This includes a complete, time-stamped event log showing activity for each responding unit
  • Integrated with Fire MDT to provide responders real-time CAD data from within their vehicles
  • Equipped with a Master Location function, which allows for preplanned reports to be completed
  • Designed with complete call logs available within the Fire RMS immediately upon call creation in the CAD
  • Featuring event details pre-populated in the NFIRS report, eliminating duplicate data entry and errors
  • Featuring FEMA-certified NFIRS reporting with automatic NFIRS validation and report submission to the State
  • Able to manage all department activities from Fire RMS reporting, scheduling, personnel training, inventory management, and much more in one system

The Results

  • Significant yearly cost savings
  • Single CAD platform to seamlessly perform a variety of tasks
  • Integrated CAD and RMS systems for data sharing and streamlined workflow
  • Extensible platform with multiple modules for added functionality
  • Elimination of duplicate CFS entries by police and fire dispatchers
  • Time saved and increased documentation accuracy
As with any of our clients, CSI provides Jersey City with unparalleled around-the-clock technical support and frequent virtual and on-site visits to ensure that our valued clients are getting the most out of CSI’s software solutions.

Total Solution Powered by InfoShare® Engine

Long gone are the days of entering the same data or searching for information on multiple systems. With CSI’s Total Public Safety Solution, Jersey City now benefits from true inter-agency integration. All cases and records, situational awareness, location data, and other information are seamlessly shared between CAD, RMS, MDT, and Fire RMS in real-time. Integrated systems have the advantage of increased productivity, communication, and service; and, in the long run, they keep first responders safe.

All CSI application, modules, and submodules are powered by our patented InfoShare® Engine, a low-code development platform designed for maximum adaptability and integration. We believe that agencies should be able to customize their systems to fit their workflow and requirements with minimal vendor support. Moreover, agencies using InfoShare® CAD and RMS can easily optimize their operations with modules such as:
  • eTicketing Gateway
  • Evidence and Property
  • Warrants
  • Internal Affairs
  • Policy & Procedure
  • Analytics & Crime Analysis
  • And many more
Our single total solution platform provides a one-stop, integrated environment for all public safety needs. Jersey City will expand its capabilities by adding modules such as Personnel and Scheduling, Fire Inspection, and with many more to come.

In Closing

CSI would like to express our deepest admiration and respect to the entire Jersey City Department of Public Safety. They undertook this transition with a very tight time frame, which offered no room for missteps or error. Jersey City staff and CSI staff worked shoulder to shoulder to make this amazing transformation in less than two months! Jersey City’s cooperation and dedication are a credit to the profession of public safety.

We are proud to partner with Jersey City Public Safety in providing it with top-tier public safety software and analytics, and we look forward to a successful partnership for years to come.

brief: Millersville University Police Department (MUPD) has joined CSI Technology Group’s existing Lancaster County Regional Cloud environment, bringing the total number of agencies serviced by the environment to twelve.
body:
Millersville University Police Department (MUPD) has joined CSI Technology Group’s existing Lancaster County Regional Cloud environment, bringing the total number of agencies serviced by the environment to twelve.

Millersville University was established in 1855. Its Police Department provides 24-hour coverage year-round with a full staff of sworn state-commissioned police officers to a student body of approximately 9,500 students.

By partnering with CSI, MUPD reduced their infrastructure costs, protected themselves from advanced cyber-attacks and unexpected disasters, and equipped themselves with the most advanced Records Management System (RMS) on the market.

Millersville University Police Department chose CSI earlier this year as [the provider of] our new records management system. Our officers and I are pleased with the ease of use within the system as well as their training, support, and responsiveness to us as a smaller police agency. CSI mirrors our community engagement and problem-solving mission; they understand and meet our unique patrol, investigative and administrative needs.

Pete Anders
Millersville University Chief of Police
Faced with the desire to replace their servers and their aging RMS, the University Police Department turned to CSI’s cloud migration expertise and industry-leading InfoShare® RMS.

With the application fully hosted on the cloud, MUPD is no longer burdened with server expenses, backup management, or disaster recovery. This smart decision provides them with significant cost savings and peace of mind. In addition, the Department can adopt a hands-off approach as all maintenance of the cloud environment is managed by CSI’s Network Team.

CSI has multiple County Cloud environments. The Lancaster Cloud is hosted on AWS GovCloud in their secure, CJIS-compliant government site. CSI can also host its suite of integrated software to support Police, Fire, and EMS personnel on Microsoft’s CJIS-complaint Azure Government. Both platforms are designed for maximum government security, and CSI can accommodate whichever of the two environments the client prefers.

The multi-tenant design permits the sharing of resources yet allows each agency to retain its own identity (workflows, logos, reporting, etc.) and, most importantly, control of its own data. The sharing of resources such as incident data, people, and vehicles comes at no additional cost, a result of forward-thinking in the design of our InfoShare® Engine.

For the first time, the Police Department has a CAD feed from County Dispatch, which populates information into InfoShare® RMS, speeding up incident reporting time.
To decrease time on scene, the Department interfaces with Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Law Enforcement Assistance Network (CLEAN), allowing officers to look up drivers’ license and vehicle registration information.
The information returned from queries can be pulled directly into InfoShare®, populating the appropriate fields, reducing time transcribing information, minimizing typing errors, and ultimately improving officer safety.

Looking to reduce time spent on traffic enforcement and to improve accuracy, the Department added the eTicketing gateway. This add-on module eliminates handwritten citations, improves the legibility of the citation, and once issued, electronically files the citation almost instantaneously with the Pennsylvania Court System.

Unlike a vast majority of police departments, university police departments are required by federal law to compile complex statistics on crimes that occur on and around school property. This is known as CLERY reporting. To streamline this arduous task, MUPD purchased the CLERY module.

Another requirement not unique to universities but not prevalent with police agencies was the ability to integrate to the University’s Single Sign-On (SSO) process. As a custom project, CSI was able to fulfill the University IT’s security requirement and interface the component fully to their application.

Officers of MUPD standing in front of Winter Center

We at CSI are pleased that after conducting evaluations of potential records management solutions, the Department chose InfoShare® RMS over other vendor’s solutions. On behalf of the other Lancaster County agencies already members of the CSI family, we welcome the Millersville University Police Department and look forward to a long and successful partnership.

title: Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Module
shareTitle: Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Module
brief: CSI Technology Group’s new Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Module was released and is now available to New Jersey County Prosecutor's Offices.
body:
CSI Technology Group’s new Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Module was released and is now available to New Jersey County Prosecutor's Offices. This module was specifically created in response to the Marijuana Decriminalization & Cannabis Legalization bills that Governor Phil Murphy signed into law on Feb. 22, 2021. Additional clarifying provisions concerning parental notification of juveniles were added on Mar. 26, 2021.

Underage individuals found unlawfully possessing or consuming marijuana, cannabis, hashish, or alcohol receive a written warning on their first offense. At first, parental notification was only required on the second offense, but that has since been revised. To discourage minors from using marijuana and alcohol, law enforcement officers are required to issue a written warning and notify the parent or guardian after the first violation. Subsequent violations come with written warnings and a referral to community treatment services.

Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Summary Page

This new module is part of the InfoShare® Juvenile suite of products that will give local law enforcement agencies and prosecutors’ offices the tools needed to record and track underage usage and provide written warnings.

Key features of this module:
  • Create and document warnings in a secure database
  • Capture underage persons information
  • Record parent(s) and guardian information
  • Collect offence information
  • Generate the appropriate warning forms with officer’s signature
  • Forward warnings to the prosecutor’s office for notification, retention, and purging when the retention period is satisfied
The Underage Marijuana/Alcohol Warning Module allows for the local law enforcement officer to quickly gather juvenile, parent/guardian, and offence information as well as determine if this was a first or subsequent offence. Depending on the situation, the officer can quickly create the necessary warning form or the appropriate Possession with Intent to Distribute Sworn Statement.

The Prosecutor’s Office will retain the warnings for future reference and after a set period of time, the underage warning will be purged from the system as required by law.

That’s why CSI Technology Group teamed up with fire professionals and local enforcement agencies to design a comprehensive solution to streamline fire inspections and maintain up-to-date premise records.

Our Fire Prevention Bureau contracted with InfoShare® to generate a new, state-of-the-art, fire prevention system with an eye toward customization and fulfilling our specific needs. We persevered as a team and now enjoy the multi-faceted features of the InfoShare® system. In our humble opinion, InfoShare® is the true “Cadillac” of the fire prevention system software arena.

Andrew Chiurazzi, Fire Official & Michael Valente, Chief Fire Inspector
Palisades Park Bureau of Fire Prevention
InfoShare® Fire Inspection is a mobile and web-based paperless inspection and report document management module for local and state agencies. Our solution combines fire inspection, records management, mobile operations, and a public portal into a single integrated platform. It simplifies inspections through:
  • Paperless reporting with electronic signatures
  • Report, document, and permit management
  • Customizable inspection worksheets/checklists
  • Inspection assignment, scheduling, and recordkeeping
  • Intuitive, professional, and easy-to-use interface
  • Integrated mapping for inspection route navigation

Moreover, this module facilitates collaboration by enabling direct coordination and notification with other officials.

InfoShare® Fire Inspection was created with compliance, control, and customizability in mind. We have a licensed agreement with the International Code Council (ICC) to keep current with the Uniform Fire Code, making sure that our systems are fully compliant with the latest standards in fire prevention and safety. In terms of accessibility, each agency maintains its own files for each property, building, premise, or facility that requires an inspection and/or permit—users can track this data how they want, when they want, and where they want. Inspection reports, notices and/or orders, images, complaints, and other documentation are stored in the approved PDF/A format consistent with the State of New Jersey’s records management standards. We can also customize the system to meet the requirements and workflow of agencies located in other states.

InfoShare® Fire Inspection Report Sample

With a complete list of preloaded codes, standards, and local ordinances, InfoShare® Fire Inspection is a robust report system with the flexibility to serve the needs of fire officials and inspectors in any municipality, regardless of size. All required state reports/forms can be customized to the needs of the agency. Agencies can build their own templates, forms, and specific in-house documents. To streamline the reporting process, electronic signatures are automatically applied to all forms, reports, and documents. InfoShare® Fire Inspection also provides a built-in validation tool that helps inspectors review all violations before issuing any orders. The fire code database is current with the 2015 NJIFC violations and flexible enough to handle any specific ordinance violations.
