title: New Hampshire State Police: Working Together to Build an Integrated New Hampshire-Centric System
shareTitle: New Hampshire State Police: Working Together to Build an Integrated New Hampshire-Centric System
brief: “This was by far the most professional and thorough review process that I have ever gone through in my 14 years with the company,” explained Richard Norcross, Executive Vice President of CSI Technology Group, “they did their homework.”
body:
“This was by far the most professional and thorough review process that I have ever gone through in my 14 years with the company,” explained Richard Norcross, Executive Vice President of CSI Technology Group, “they did their homework.”

In 2018, the State of New Hampshire acting through the Department of Safety (NHDOS) released a request for proposal to procure a new software package that would provide the New Hampshire State Police (NHSP) with an integrated Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Record Management System (RMS) that would support all state police operations. It became immediately obvious during the procurement process that the NHDOS knew exactly what they wanted.

Searching for a Fully Integrated Solution

Compared to other demos that lasted only a few hours with little guidance on specific issues, the demo with NHDOS lasted several days and involved significant hands-on participation by a committee of 20+ end users. Using our proprietary low code technology, we quickly developed a New Hampshire-centric system and converted several of their reports prior to the demo. Delivering features at a later date was not an option. Right then and there, they wanted to know what our system could do. They ran detailed, complex scenarios for the New Hampshire State Police, the New Hampshire Marine Patrol, the New Hampshire Fire Marshal’s Office, and the New Hampshire Fish & Game Department to ensure that our system could handle the full breadth of their operations. We showed how our InfoShare® Total Solution brought all the divisions of the NHDOS together under one system that was natively built to work together and that could continually adapt to each division’s evolving needs.

NHSP Communication Center CAD Stations

The NH State Police was searching for an intuitive, browser-based, and fully integrated solution that met the modern needs of law enforcement. State troopers from different units and divisions needed the ability to share data and access mission-critical information in real-time.

Key system requirements included:
  • A single, fully integrated CAD, RMS, and MDT solution from a single vendor
  • Data sharing, accessibility, and interoperability between all systems
  • Interfaces with existing NHSP systems and external systems
  • CJIS- and NBIRS-compliant system with role-based security permissions
  • Secure cloud-hosted environment with vendor support and maintenance
In addition to these requirements, the NHSP was looking for a long-term partner who shared their vision of a truly interoperable system. The partnership would require a strong commitment from both parties. The system would first need to be built, then refined, and then continuously adapted to changing needs. “It’s important to us that our software reflects the local identity and customs and flavor,” said Richard Norcross. Even though CSI was not established yet in the State of New Hampshire, the NHSP was impressed with our technology and our willingness to work together as a team to deliver a system that would meet their needs today and in the future.

The Granite State

With a population of 1.36 million, the state of New Hampshire borders Canada to the north, Vermont to the west, Maine to the east, and Massachusetts to the south with 18 miles of Atlantic Ocean shoreline in the southeast corner of the state. The state has 221 towns, 13 cities, 10 counties, and 23 unincorporated places along with 950 public lakes, ponds, rivers, and streams. The southern and eastern parts of the state contain the most population density with the state becoming more rural and less populous the further north into the white mountain region to the Canadian border.

The New Hampshire State Police

The mission of the NH State Police is to provide the highest degree of law enforcement service throughout the State of New Hampshire while maintaining the traditions of fairness, professionalism, and integrity. Commanded by Colonel Nathan Noyes, the division is comprised of 544 employees of which there are 360 uniformed troopers. It is divided into six regional troops (A-F) and Troop G charged with enforcing statewide motor carrier regulations. Responsibilities include traffic management, field operations, motor carrier management, major crime and narcotics investigations, motor vehicle crash and reconstruction, maritime law enforcement for inland bodies of water, explosive ordinance disposal, SWAT and K9 operations, and emergency service dispatch for multiple third-party municipalities.

NHSP CAD Workstation

Fragmentation and Data Silos

The NHSP relied on a legacy CAD/RMS system installed in 2008 that was no longer meeting compliance standards or operational needs. Data was siloed in various locations, and some of the units had their own individual databases. There was no function to search other databases so troopers had to call one another to obtain the necessary data, significantly reducing the efficiency of their operations. Combining statistics at the end of the month was another challenge because there was no single data repository. All of the databases needed to be consolidated into one fully searchable data repository to ensure the data is readily available to all users. Some units had their own reporting processes. Other units used separate systems that were built in-house or built by other vendors. The biggest problem was that these systems were not designed to talk to each other.

Joining the CSI Family

On November 21st, 2019, the State of New Hampshire acquired our InfoShare® operating system on a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) basis. And on June 27th, 2021, the system was deployed across all units in the NH State Police. With the new system, NHSP benefits from the following functionalities:
  • Fully integrated, cloud-hosted CAD, RMS, and Mobile system
  • Single data repository with master indices
  • Custom mapping layers and AVL capabilities
  • Accurate address and location services
  • Integrated eTicket and Electronic Crash Management Records system
  • Robust ad-hoc, NIBRS, and administrative reporting
  • Flexible group-, role-, or case-based permission settings
  • Crime mapping, analytics, and link analysis
  • And many more
The New Hampshire State Police, the New Hampshire Marine Patrol, the New Hampshire Fire Marshal’s Office, and the New Hampshire Fish & Game Department now all operate out of the InfoShare® system. Each division is no longer running its operations on its own individual, siloed systems. Now, all divisions have the capability of sharing information back and forth.

CSI has been very accommodating working in concert with the NHSP team to configure our RMS and MDT platforms to match our unique agency needs and continue to refine the platform and work as a cohesive team on future phases of the project.

Captain Vic Muzzey
New Hampshire State Police
There were also several State of New Hampshire-specific interfaces that the new CAD and RMS system would need to integrate to include Justice-One Network Environment (J-ONE), Electronic Citation (E-Citation), and Electronic Crash Reporting (E-Crash). J-One was designed by the State of New Hampshire to create an interconnected network of criminal justice information that is accessible and shared between various components of the criminal justice system throughout the state. It creates a seamless flow of data from one component of the criminal justice system to another that is both timely and complete and available to all criminal justice stakeholders. The development of E-Crash and E-Citation also provides timely data on citation and crash reports through J-ONE to agencies such as the Department of Motor Vehicles as well as the state’s court system.

Converting 13 Years of Legacy Data

Using our comprehensive, structured data conversion service, we consolidated 13 individual legacy databases into one single, fully searchable data repository. Our data conversion team analyzed 13 years of data from the legacy vendor as well as the other databases from the different divisions and converted them into our data structure. The data is not simply copied but also cleansed, condensed, and standardized. From the user’s perspective, the legacy data appears as if it was entered originally in the new system. There’s no need to search a separate database or use a portal to access the legacy data. “The NHSP was extremely impressed with how that was done and the results. We went through a review process with them, and they reviewed selected cases over the years to match up. We brought over all of their photographs, attachments, documents that were in the old system and brought them into the new system as well as the data related to them,” explained Peter Ugalde, Director of the CAD/RMS Division at CSI Technology Group.

Intermixing the legacy data with the new data allows users to draw logical connections and merge cases together so that one person or vehicle is organized under one single entry that can be shared across events. Now that all the data has been consolidated under one single database, troopers can easily search, retrieve, and review information themselves without having to call other units or divisions. Moreover, compiling crime statistics and performance tracking reports can be easily done with just a few clicks.

SaaS Model and Cloud Hosting

One of NHSP’s requirements was to outsource the hosting, system maintenance, and database administration to the vendor. With InfoShare® Cloud and our SaaS infrastructure, the NHSP system is now hosted on the CJIS-compliant AWS GovCloud at a fraction of the cost of traditional CAD/RMS systems. The benefits of our cloud-based SaaS CAD/RMS include:
  • FBI CJIS-compliant security and encryption
  • Significant cost savings in the long-term
  • Maintenance, updates, backup, and testing are handled by CSI
  • Superior redundancy and disaster preparedness and recovery
  • “Anywhere, anytime” accessibility from agency-approved devices
  • Flexible customization by configuring the system in the cloud
  • Real-time data sharing

The Future with New Hampshire State Police

Our work with the NHSP has entered the second phase. And we continue to work together to make adjustments and enhancements to the InfoShare® base operating system as necessary. Additional modules and functionalities we’ve recently deployed or are in the midst of deploying include:
  • 23 CFR Part 23 compliant Intelligence module
  • Personnel & Training module
  • Permits & Licensing module
  • Send cases to NH Department of Justice or County Attorneys/Prosecutors

RMS Training Day with Troopers

Due to the successful partnership with NHSP, we’re also working on expanding our presence in the state of New Hampshire. “The lessons learned from working with the New Hampshire State Police have greatly aided us with other law enforcement agencies around the state. Our next step is to link all these agencies together for data sharing purposes, officer safety, and solving crimes,” said Richard Norcross. So far, our new partners in New Hampshire include:
  • University of New Hampshire Police and contracted municipal police, fire, and ambulance service agencies
  • Grafton County Police Department and Fire Department
  • Hanover Police Department and Fire Department
  • Plaistow Police Department and Fire Department
  • Merrimack Police Department and Fire Department
  • Bedford Police Department and Fire Department
Building this regional connectivity in New Hampshire will greatly enhance data and intelligence sharing between agencies at the local level and the state level. Each agency will be able to search, view, and share data with each other without needing any direct contact and/or formal requests. At the same time, each agency still has complete control of its own data, meaning that it can choose what to share and who to share the information with.

Keys to a Successful Partnership

When asked why this partnership has been successful, Peter Ugalde responded, “The partnership between state police and CSI’s deployment teams is what makes this project a success. Without so many people in the NHSP having a vested interest, it would have been a lot more difficult.”

The deployment wasn’t necessarily easy. Even though we had trained every single member of the State Police for several months prior to deployment, inevitably, there were a few grumblings in the first 2-3 weeks. To make the transition as smooth as possible, NHSP organized a team of ~30 troopers that they called their technical team. They were the subject matter experts serving as the first line of support. If a trooper had any questions, they would call someone from the technical team for assistance. “I thought it was phenomenal that they brought together this group,” said Peter Ugalde. He concludes, “One of the things that I was very proud of is that the commissioners and some higher-ups in the State Police said that it’s extremely unusual to have a group of people work together on a project as long as we did and still have a good relationship that we maintain with them on a daily basis.”

We look forward to the future phases of this project and hope to have a successful ongoing partnership with the New Hampshire State Police for years to come.

title: Successful Public-Private Collaboration: Creating the Daniel’s Law System with NJDCA
shareTitle: Successful Public-Private Collaboration: Creating the Daniel’s Law System with NJDCA
brief: Following the tragic death of Daniel Anderl, the late son of Judge Esther Salas, Governor Murphy signed Daniel’s Law in November 2020.
body:
Following the tragic death of Daniel Anderl, the late son of Judge Esther Salas, Governor Murphy signed Daniel’s Law in November 2020. This new law amends the Open Public Records Act (OPRA) to prohibit the disclosure of home addresses and other personal information of Covered Persons—former, active, and retired judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officers, and their immediate family members—on websites controlled by state, county, and local government agencies.

The assailant easily found Judge Salas’ personal information on the internet and used it to target her and her family in their own home. This goes to show how vulnerable public officials are in the digital age and how important Daniel’s Law is in adding a layer of security and protection from potential threats and/or attacks for public servants and their families.

The New Jersey Department of Community Affairs (NJDCA) got to work straight away and created the Office of Information Privacy (OIP) to carry out the work of complying with Daniel’s Law. There was no time to waste and lives were at stake. Christine Campbell, who previously served as the Deputy Chief Technology Officer for Legal and Compliance at the New Jersey Office of Information Technology (NJOIT), was appointed to lead the newly-formed OIP.

The project officially kicked off on January 17th, 2022, and the system went live on July 12th, 2022. Within 6 months, the NJDCA along with the Attorney General’s Office, the Office of Information Technology, and various other NJ public agencies collaborated with CSI Technology Group to create an entirely new system from scratch. Together, we created an Online Portal allowing Covered Persons to request the redaction of their personal information from public records and internet postings. During the first week of registration, the Daniel’s Law Portal accepted over 1,300 requests for redaction, and the number continues to grow.

When asked why CSI was selected for this project, Richard Norcross, Executive Vice President, couldn’t contain how proud he was of the team, “CSI has been a company that’s been around for 30 years. We were chosen because of our track record, because of our history of successful deliveries, and because of our history of executing challenging projects on time. This was definitely a challenging project because of all the nuances. They had a law that was written with no guidance on how to implement it.” There were multiple brainstorming sessions between Richard Norcross’ team and the team led by John Harrison, the Director of Information Technology at the NJDCA. They discussed all the stakeholders that had to be involved in this project and mapped out the complex workflows involving various public agencies. From those discussions, they envisioned a new system that would successfully implement Daniel’s Law.

Once the diagrams were clearly laid out, the scope of work was quickly drafted and approved in the State Government in record time. “We have proven to the State of New Jersey and other States time and time again that they can give us a problem that they need to solve with technology, and we can take their concept, their ideas, their rough architecture and create a working product that will meet and, in many cases, exceed what they expected.”

Qualified individuals can register for their Daniel’s Law account and link it to their MyNewJersey account at https://danielslaw.nj.gov/. MyNewJersey is a system that allows businesses and citizens to use a single ID to access many services such as pension & benefits, payroll information, taxes, permits, etc. Working with the OIP, we integrated the Online Portal into the MyNewJersey Portal to give people a single point of entry for security and convenience. CSI also designed a vetting process that involves verifying employment and qualifications electronically by partnering with the New Jersey Department of the Treasury and the United States Department of Justice. One of the requirements that the State made was not wanting to collect all the information if a person did not qualify, so we created a two-step process in order to ensure the applicants qualify before collecting and assigning redaction information to the appropriate authorities. Once the information is retrieved and the agencies redact the information from the necessary places, a notification is sent to the applicant.

CSI not only delivered on time but also delivered on budget. The Daniel’s Law system is a case study of successful public-private collaboration—the result of many key persons and key agencies working together toward the delivery of the system. CSI was able to deliver when it mattered most because of:
  • Experience: Efficient processes in place for drafting the scope of work, making the scope of work understandable for the clients, and preparing documentation for the engineers. Making sure the scope of work covers all bases ensures that the project starts early.
  • Decision Making: A leadership team with a flat management style prevents bureaucracy and layers of review that inevitably builds unnecessary delays in the project.
  • Subject Matter Expertise: 80% of account managers and management at CSI worked in the public sector, giving us an extraordinary advantage in dealing with government problems, managing government projects, and understanding the client’s needs quickly.
  • Communication: Our clients are our partners. Constant daily communication, weekly meetings, and in-person demos with clients and their constituents help move the project forward and alleviate any concerns. We make sure that all stakeholders are comfortable with what we’re doing and how we’re doing it.
  • Technology: At the heart of every CSI application is our patented InfoShare® Engine, a flexible low-code development system that our engineers are specifically trained to work with. Our engineers are able to take complicated processes and build them out efficiently as well as quickly configure the system to address ever-changing needs.
What happens after the system is deployed? Richard Norcross explains, “Just as important is our phenomenal reputation for our aftercare. Even after we go live, we still meet with folks to discuss things, take in ideas, and make things quicker, faster, smoother.” John Porter, Deputy Director of the County/State Agency Division at CSI, explains the aftercare in the context of Daniel’s Law, “During the first four weeks, we were updating the system daily based on client and end-user feedback to make it as efficient as possible to submit and process registrations. After receiving a request from the client, I meet with the engineers to develop an interim solution. They get it coded, and we review it with the client—all within 24 hours.”

Offering his perspective, Joshua Ottenberg, Director of the County/State Agency Division at CSI, adds, “It's a huge compliment when the phone rings and it's the government calling, and they say we need you to help us solve a problem—that doesn’t happen to a lot of companies. Our subject matter expertise puts us in a position to not only help with the technology, but we’re also on the ground floor building the requirements, building the solution from the ground up, and building the relationships between the government agencies to make this project happen.”

Speaking about the larger context of Daniel’s Law, Ottenberg explains, “All across the country and all across the world, governments are taking citizen privacy on the Internet much more seriously. Daniel’s Law is a way of regulating that problem and giving people certain rights and protections. But it’s not the only way. So what we’re building here will be replicated in many other states with local variations, which is necessary to make it work politically and legally in those places. But the fact remains that CSI brings true subject matter expertise to manage these types of projects in a way that other companies can’t.”

To access the online portal, visit: DanielsLaw.nj.gov

title: Somerset County Sheriff’s Office Modernizes Records Management System to Support County-Wide Data Sharing
shareTitle: Somerset County Sheriff’s Office Modernizes Records Management System to Support County-Wide Data Sharing
brief: Somerset County Sheriff’s Office (SCSO) replaces its legacy system with a modern and reliable RMS system provided by CSI Technology Group.
body:
Somerset County Sheriff’s Office (SCSO) replaces its legacy system with a modern and reliable RMS system provided by CSI Technology Group. With the addition of Somerset County, CSI now services 43% of all Sheriff’s Offices in the state of New Jersey.

In addition to Public Safety solutions, CSI also designs powerful systems for Courts and Justice agencies such as Prosecutor’s and District Attorney’s Offices, Attorney General’s Offices, and Public Defender Offices. As an established partner with CSI, Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office staff recommended that SCSO examine the InfoShare® system during their search for a new vendor. Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office personnel shared their experience with CSI as a vendor and how reliable CSI’s eProsecution solution was.

Sheriff Darrin J. Russo Leading the Somerset County Sheriff’s Office

Implementing a Highly Customized System and Training Program

At the request of SCSO, CSI was tasked to build a single-solution RMS with granular data sharing capabilities. SCSO provides view-only access to its data to other branches in the county, including the Somerset County Jail and the Somerset County Communications Center. These branches can look up master names registered in the SCSO RMS and then run their own processes such as obtaining pertinent information, checking active warrants, or running NCIC queries. Promoting this kind of data sharing results in a more efficient and safer experience for all public safety professionals in the county. Another unique point of this project is that the SCSO is a highly specialized agency with very specific needs, which meant that the system, the training, and the interfaces had to be uniquely customized to serve SCSO’s mission.

With our InfoShare® Engine, a low code development platform for government ERP applications, CSI configured the system to easily fulfill SCSO’s unique requirements. Unlike other vendors, who typically charge high customization costs, CSI developed its own proprietary system to deploy an agency-customized system at a fraction of the cost and in a fraction of the time as well.

Customized Training Program for the SCSO staff

Like the system, the training program was also customized to SCSO’s specific operations. “Once I learned there were also clerical people who have varying areas of responsibility, some doing only warrant data entry, we customized the training to exactly what they were going to be doing on a daily basis. I was once a police officer, and I was in their shoes, so that experience helps me understand what the little nuances would be and what would make them frustrated. It all starts with listening,” recounts Matthew Edwards, one of our experienced RMS account managers. The InfoShare® RMS comes with many features, but not every officer or staff member will need to use all those features. He explains, “We didn’t cloud their head with all this information for things that were not in their job description or duties. Because we geared the training to exactly what they will be doing day in and day out, they walked out of the training feeling refreshed. In the first two days of going live, I knew they had retained a lot of the information because they were already doing their jobs proficiently. They had entered numerous warrants without my help or the Sergeant’s help.”

CSI is not in the business of providing cookie-cutter versions of our software to as many agencies as possible. Part of our deployment process involves understanding thoroughly what our clients do, how they do it, and what they really need. Features and sections in the system can be turned on and off to make it cleaner, neater, and user-friendly. We want to make sure that we’re not delivering software that’s overly built for their agency. We want our clients to feel they have control of the system. After all, our clients own the system, and we make sure they understand that we can activate certain features for them at any time.

State-of-the-Art CSI InfoShare® System Replaces an Outdated Application

SCSO is responsible for central booking, master name indexing, bias crimes in jail, investigations, court security, and delivering warrants for cases in Somerset County. Their legacy system was becoming increasingly outdated, and they had serious concerns that the system would fail. They were looking for a modern and reliable system that was easy to use with easy access to records. One of the issues with the older system was that their data was split into three different silos. In their search for a new reliable system, they were looking for a more seamless flow of information. They wanted to be able to access all the information—booking, arrest data, and warrants—efficiently in one place instead of jumping from one silo to the next.

Choosing CSI as a Partner

When asked why SCSO chose CSI as a vendor, Thomas Koundry, Deputy Director of the CAD/RMS Division, responded, “They were very familiar with other vendors and what they had and what was going on throughout the county. They invited us to a meeting with their command staff to question us, look at our capabilities, and see our system in action. Talking to us and seeing what we could offer them right then and there gave them that comfort level.” Matthew Edwards added, “We showed the stakeholders in the room, exactly what our application did and what it could do compared to what they know of our competitors, and they were very impressed.”

By partnering with CSI, SCSO benefits from the following:
  • Modern, reliable, and future-proof system
  • County-wide data sharing with other agencies
  • Easy access to data with no duplicate entries
  • NIBRS reporting
  • Expert data conversion and interfacing services
  • And more

Key Interfaces and the AOC eCDR Feed

There are several interfaces that will greatly improve SCSO’s operations. One of the most important interfaces CSI has built for them is the Live Scan interface. Much of the agency’s job involves registering arrest and applicant data, biometrics, fingerprints, palm prints, photos, and tattoos. Prior to CSI, the agency would have to enter this data twice, once during the initial screening and once more when entering the data into their legacy RMS. Now, all the Live Scan data is electronically fed into InfoShare® RMS, completely removing any duplicate data entry whilst also eliminating potential typing errors. The CJP interface is also a big convenience for the SCSO. They are now able to send their indictable cases to the Prosecutor’s Office electronically. The NCIC/DMV interface will save the agency a lot of time. The law enforcement officer can enter a driver’s license or license plate number into the RMS and run NCIC/DMV queries. Not only does this result in improved situational awareness but also the data from the DMV is prepopulated back into the RMS.

Somerset County Sheriff’s Office Police Vehicle

Lastly, the AOC eCDR feed will be a game-changer. “If a criminal complaint is generated, it goes to the Prosecutor’s Office electronically. But currently, it stops there. Now we’re going to channel the criminal complaint data through an interface from the Prosecutor’s Office to the local level, being the Sheriff’s Office,” explains Matthew Edwards, “The biggest benefit is now when you put the information into a criminal complaint, there are indicators that say, ‘Has the person been fingerprinted yet? Are they in jail? What are the criminal charges? What’s the date of the arrest? What’s the municipality?’ All that information is prepopulated. Since they are responsible for central booking for the whole county, this data is very valuable to them. They are entrusted with managing every person who’s ever been arrested in Somerset County on a daily basis and following up if necessary.”

Thomas Koundry says, “We’re very happy and very proud to partner with Somerset County Sheriff’s Office on this eCDR feed. The SCSO will be the only non-prosecutorial, non-prosecutor’s-office law enforcement agency in the state of New Jersey that will be receiving this feed. We are grateful to pilot this with such a professional organization.”

The Future with Somerset County Sheriff’s Office

There are still many opportunities to explore with the Somerset County Sheriff’s Office. The future is very promising, and as we work together, we’ll figure out how to expand their capabilities even further. It’s been a fantastic partnership so far and we’re looking forward to many strong years of success together.

title: New Hampshire North Country Interoperability Consortium: Creating a Fully Interoperable CAD-to-CAD System
shareTitle: New Hampshire North Country Interoperability Consortium: Creating a Fully Interoperable CAD-to-CAD System
brief: In New Hampshire, CSI has built a fully interoperable CAD-to-CAD system customized to meet the needs of the North Country Interoperability Consortium communication centers located in Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln.
body:
In New Hampshire, CSI has built a fully interoperable CAD-to-CAD system customized to meet the needs of the North Country Interoperability Consortium communication centers located in Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln. We combined their disparate CAD, RMS, and MDT systems for Police, Fire, and EMS from different vendors into a single system that can handle all emergency needs, from simple to complex calls for service.

The consortium of public safety communication centers can now seamlessly communicate and coordinate with one another to serve a large geographic area that extends beyond New Hampshire to include Vermont.

The North Country Interoperability Consortium

The Grafton County Dispatch Center is operated through the Grafton County Sheriff’s Department and serves all of the towns in Grafton County and all of the Twin Fire Mutual Aid towns, which include Orange County and Caledonia County in Vermont. Hanover is a regional dispatch center that covers Dartmouth College as well as several municipalities in Grafton County and some municipalities in the state of Vermont for fire and EMS service. Together, these two regional communication centers cover a large geography and support dispatching services for a total of 23 Law Enforcement agencies and 44 Fire & EMS agencies. The Lincoln Dispatch Center is operated by the Lincoln Police Department and provides services to Woodstock Police Department as well as fire departments.

In 2019, Hanover began to search for a replacement for our 20-year-old CAD/RMS system. Some of our requirements were simple: (1) connection to NH J-ONE, (2) cloud-based platform with remote access, and (3) connectivity to neighboring agencies and the NHSP. After reviewing several software packages, their costs, their features, and their functionality, we, in conjunction with the regional consortium, decided on a shared system utilizing CSI’s InfoShare® platform... We’re excited to continue to grow our system with CSI in the future.

E. Douglas Hackett
Communications Coordinator
Hanover Police Department
Grafton, Hanover, and Lincoln wanted to run their dispatching services concurrently with one another. They envisioned a system with three-way communication, coordination, and data sharing capabilities. They needed to redirect calls for service and bridge multiple agencies from different regions for safe emergency response and efficient dispatch routing. However, prior to contracting with CSI, data sharing was limited to contacts, and redirecting calls required dispatchers to pick up the phone and call the other dispatch center. To make matters worse, their previous vendor seemed unwilling or incapable to provide updates to the system, and its customer service left much to be desired. These limitations caused them significant operational problems, which prompted a search for a new vendor.

The consortium cast a very wide net during the procurement process. They looked at 14 different systems from multiple vendors before selecting CSI. When asked why they chose to partner with us, Richard Norcross, Vice President of CSI, responded, “They were looking for something newer that would better satisfy their modern policing needs. The fact that we listened to their requirements and specific nuances of working up in that section of New Hampshire and Vermont was a big selling point. But probably the most important feature was the CAD-to-CAD communication.” He continues, “They needed a vendor that understood the importance of building an interoperable system that would allow the two communication centers to work off one another and act as failovers for each other. Each center would know what the other center was doing.”

Benefits of Partnering with CSI

By partnering with CSI and unifying their dispatch centers as well as public safety systems, the North Country Interoperability Consortium benefits from the following:
  • Integrated CAD, RMS, and Mobile systems for Police, Fire, and EMS
  • Products and modules designed from the ground up to natively work together
  • Highly configurable and expandable system to meet current and future needs
  • Improved communication, coordination, and data sharing
  • More resources to handle increased call volumes
  • Faster response times and better service
  • Superior major incident management involving multiple resources
  • Cost sharing and shared grant and funding opportunities
In addition, Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln made an informed decision to migrate their operations to the cloud. “They wanted to use InfoShare® Cloud because I had explained to them the benefits—seamless data sharing for the CAD-to-CAD, better stability, automatic backups, and the fact that we provided a total service of maintaining the software and servers,” explained Richard Norcross. Essentially, Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln chose to leave all the server maintenance, hosting, and database administration to CSI so that they could focus on higher priority tasks.

“They were very interested in the Software-as-a-Service pricing model. And they had a great deal of confidence in our ability to maintain the product, maintain the cloud, and eliminate any concerns they had about fires, floods, and other possible disasters,” he concluded. In short, by migrating to the cloud, Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln will have:
  • Seamless data sharing between systems
  • Improved system stability and performance
  • Significant cost savings in storage, maintenance, and deployment
  • Vendor hosting, support, backup, updates, and maintenance
  • Exceptional redundancy and disaster preparedness and recovery
  • FBI CJIS-compliant security and encryption

As part of a large regional consortium, we serve multiple police, fire, and EMS agencies across four counties in two states. We went live a year ago and thousands of CFS have been processed in CAD, shared to a solid MDT platform, and processed in the RMS. CSI has met our expectations for our initial project and more. They invested in our future success by hiring five local people who are dedicated to our little, rural part of the country and are always available for not only any issue that may come up, but also to ensure development is based on actual field-user needs and experience. Support is immediate, and working relationships are built and maintained.

Tom Andross
Director of Communications
Grafton County Sheriff’s Department

Delivering Maximum Value with Data Migration, Interfacing, and Modules

As with all of our clients, the data conversion services we offer are second to none in the public safety market. Instead of simply adding a front-end to the old system and linking it to the new system, we clean and consolidate the old data. Peter Ugalde, Director of the CAD/RMS Division, explained it as follows, “We’re analyzing and cleaning the old data and then integrating it into the new tables that we have in our system, and we integrate that data directly as if it was entered into our system for the first time. I don’t know many other vendors that do it that way.”

With Hanover, 18 years' worth of data was converted, and with Grafton County, 22 years. “When they finally saw the converted data, they had a huge sense of relief. They felt 100% better now that they had seen what we had been explaining to them. They just needed to see it in person. They were very impressed with how all the legacy data and new data were mixed seamlessly together,” said Gregory Ferry, one of our New Hampshire Account Managers.

Grafton County Dispatcher Enters a Call

CSI has considerable experience in building interfaces with a range of internal and external data sources to promote data sharing. One of the interfaces CSI built specifically for this project was the RapidSOS interface to import mobile cell phone location data directly into InfoShare® CAD. Scott Plumer, one of our New Hampshire Account Managers, explained, “One element Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln really liked was the RapidSOS interface. Having that part of their CAD system immediately changed things as before they had to log into the RapidSOS website and view the location data. Now, they appreciate how everything is integrated into one system.”

Other critical interfaces implemented for Hanover, Grafton, and Lincoln include:
  • 9-1-1 ANI/ALI Interface
  • IDEMIA - LiveScan Interface
  • TEMSIS/SIREN by Image Trends Interface
  • NH J-ONE Interface
In addition to the core public safety products, they added the Fugitive/Warrant Management module, the InfoServe Civil Process Service module, the Evidence module, the eTicketing module, and the Fire Safety and Inspection module.

Feedback from End Users

Our account managers work very closely with clients, talking regularly to sheriffs, dispatchers, police officers, and firefighters. Before going live, Gregory Ferry and Scott Plumer spent several weeks at the client site for training purposes. Scott Plumer recalls being in Hanover for three weeks, sharing “What we found were a lot of eager and excited people. But sometimes people get overwhelmed with the change depending on their level of expertise or abilities. We worked with them through it and it built up their confidence. Overall, it was a very positive training experience.”

When asked how our system improved the end user’s day-to-day, Gregory Ferry said, “The fact that all the data from CAD and MDT are pushed to the RMS, they really liked that feature. They also loved how the NCIC returns are automatically pushed to the RMS in a PDF format that doesn’t require a manual push at all, how everything is housed in one place in the RMS including the dispatch, and how easy it is to generate reports or District Court complaints because all the information is right there. We received a lot of positive responses and comments from the user level related to that.”

Our experience with CSI couldn’t have been more successful. From sales to training, CSI staff have been thorough, informative, and especially knowledgeable! The 2-week training was organized and extremely helpful, including their willingness to stay after hours to help those on later shifts. The greatest part is the client support. CSI believes in their product and supports it well. The communication between user and support is clear and timely. We would recommend this product to other agencies. No matter the size of the agency, you feel like a priority to them.

Kara Baker
Lincoln Police Department
As a customer-oriented organization, we also wanted to know if there were any challenges. “The common thing was that they all understood that it was just going to take some time getting the repetitions in to use the system. We also function differently than their previous vendor. They used to have accident reports with their own case numbers, arrest reports with their own case numbers, and so forth. They liked it better now that they could simply have one case number to use for multiple reports. It made it a lot easier for them. They no longer had to call dispatch to get a case number. They could do their own call for service if somebody walked into the police station to report vandalism, for example,” reported Scott Plumer.

Talking about CSI’s reputation and our customer service, Gregory Ferry said, “What I’ve heard from some people who have spoken to other agencies about our company, they said that there’s one thing for sure: if you need something, pick up the phone, CSI is going to answer, and they’re going to address your question and look for a solution.”

The First Days of Going Live

It didn’t take long for Hanover or Grafton to have an opportunity to stress test the system in the real world. On the very first day of going live, they had an active shooter threat with a former student on school grounds at a high school. “Backup came in from other jurisdictions in the region, and Hanover was able to see these units. Grafton County could see what was going on in Hanover,” recounts Richard Norcross, “the next day, they had a multi-alarm fire with the same situation. Fire units came in from all jurisdictions from the two communication centers, and they were able to see what was going on and what was being added to the call from both centers. This was exactly the system they envisioned in the beginning.” It was remarkable how the team at Hanover managed both high-octane crises so smoothly given that they had just learned how to use the new system. This real-world case study shows what is possible when a group of talented individuals, who take their training seriously, are united under strong leadership.

CSI Staff Collaborates with a Grafton County Dispatch Supervisor

However, it wasn’t all smooth sailing from the very beginning. As with any change, there was some initial resistance. “Before we went live, there was a lot of trepidation. There were concerns and they were nervous about certain things. They were very anxious about the go-live process. One week after the go-live, they candidly remarked that it went better than they ever could have imagined or expected. The whole tenor changed,” said Peter Ugalde.

Scott Plumer told his side of the go-live, “There was a concern that once we went live, we would get in our cars and drive home. And that was it. But after going live, I was camping out in a conference room just off their dispatch center. Having that accessibility of us there, and people coming in all the time from different agencies helped them get things moving along. We still have our weekly meetings with them to go over any questions, so we haven't gone anywhere. We’re still building this together and I think they're happy with that.”

A Long and Mutually Beneficial Partnership

Together with Grafton County, Hanover, and Lincoln, we combined their public safety systems under a single integrated solution and built a fully interoperable CAD-to-CAD system. Several new features and new projects are already in the pipeline to be rolled out soon. The future involves even more data sharing and interoperability among the different regions in New Hampshire.

title: Serving Citizens: The Transformative Effect of Automating the New Expungement System in New Jersey
shareTitle: Serving Citizens: The Transformative Effect of Automating the New Expungement System in New Jersey
brief: Having a criminal record can have a profoundly negative impact on a person’s life. Even being charged—not convicted—for a minor offense can reduce a person’s quality of life. When a person is arrested or convicted of a crime, a record is created and maintained in various law enforcement databases.
body:
Having a criminal record can have a profoundly negative impact on a person’s life. Even being charged—not convicted—for a minor offense can reduce a person’s quality of life. When a person is arrested or convicted of a crime, a record is created and maintained in various law enforcement databases. This criminal record can have significant consequences for the individual, including limiting job opportunities, housing options, and educational opportunities. In some states, a person can have difficulties getting a driver’s license and may even lose their right to vote. Bluntly put, a criminal record can be a life sentence to poverty, and as a result, bipartisan support for criminal justice reform and expungement has gathered significant momentum in several states, especially in New Jersey.

Expungement in New Jersey

In recent years, the New Jersey legislature has enacted new expungement laws, representing a significant step forward in giving individuals with criminal records a chance to start anew. For example, the Marijuana Decriminalization Law expunges the records of individuals who were once stigmatized for possessing or selling cannabis. In addition, the Clean Slate and expedited expungement programs take a proactive approach to expungement, where over a set period of time or after completing certain requirements, the state will automatically expunge selected charges from an individual’s criminal history of arrests and convictions.

Millions of records are now eligible for expungement in the state of New Jersey, but these records are not located in a single system. Whenever the state receives a request for expungement, it must locate the record(s) first across multiple state, county, and municipal databases to check the eligibility of the petition. This process is very inefficient and time-consuming. The complexity of managing and processing expungement petitions is not unique to New Jersey, as many states struggle with the same issue. With the help of InfoShare® technology, the government has made significant improvements in making the process more efficient so that citizens can receive the benefits of criminal justice reform.

Accomplishing a Herculean Feat

CSI proactively approached the New Jersey Office of the Attorney General (NJOAG), the New Jersey State Police (NJSP), and the New Jersey Administrative Office of the Courts (NJAOC) with a solution that would streamline the entire expungement process. “CSI had prior relationships that put us in a unique position with the most significant parties in the expungement workflow. We had existing interfaces and handled many of the systems for the NJSP, the NJAOC, the County Prosecutor's Offices, and the NJOAG,” recounts Richard Norcross, Executive Vice President at CSI. “But building a system that effectively connects all these agencies together is an enormous undertaking.”

After reviewing CSI’s proposal, the NJOAG, NJSP, and NJAOC agreed to work together to create a new expungement system. CSI was entrusted with this large-scale project because of our track record and domain knowledge. On top of that, because of the trust we’ve built over the years with legacy clients, CSI can facilitate cooperation among them and leverage those relationships to bring additional expertise to the project. For example, reaching out to prosecuting attorneys, who know the expungement laws inside and out, in the NJOAG and Prosecutor’s Offices across the state helped us better understand the laws and determine how the workflows have to work. Joshua Ottenberg, Director of the County/State Agency Division at CSI, observes that “There's been tremendous cooperation at all levels of government to do this, and it's been inspiring to see different agencies work together in a way that we've never really seen them work before to get the job done.”

From a technology point of view, Norcross adds, “Not only do we have the software and the InfoShare® Engine powering everything, but we also have an extremely talented group of engineers who are experts at building interfaces with third parties. We mine data out of these other systems, and we’re able to transfer that data to other agencies in a readable format, and then send them the signals back to expunge the records. If they had gone with any other vendor, it likely would have been a fragmented solution with multiple points of entry in different systems.”

Harnessing the Power of Automation

Prior to the new expungement system, NJSP staff had to go through a painstaking workflow where they had to log into a website, manually review and download the information, enter the data into their internal system, conduct separate searches across multiple systems, and manually prepare position papers. Until it was done digitally, the lack of system integration meant that information was siloed and not shared at all between systems. With New Jersey’s focus on criminal justice reform, the NJOAG, NJSP, NJAOC, and Prosecutor’s Offices needed a new system that will control and ease the increasing workload.

The most impressive feat in the New Jersey Expungement Project has been integrating the multiple systems of the NJOAG, NJSP, NJAOC, and Prosecutor’s Offices to create a single, unified system that closely follows the written statute. To help accomplish this, our team undertook the crucial task of building a number of automatic interfaces with trusted NJSP vendors and performing data integration to organize all incoming and outgoing data in a compatible format. CSI has the benefit of years of expertise in providing an adaptable and scalable total solution platform with expert interfacing to facilitate interoperability among data contributors. With our interfaces, these agencies can access multiple systems from a single point of entry and benefit from not having to re-enter existing data while simultaneously eliminating duplicate entries. Our systematic approach towards converting and cleansing data maintains the data integrity, with legacy data appearing as if it was entered natively into the new InfoShare® system.

Expungement Workflow Diagram

Automation process:

  • Citizens submit online petitions themselves, which get passed through court systems to find cases or legal reasons that would otherwise prevent expungement.
  • The petition is sent to NJSP to conduct additional checks by querying various systems.
  • If the petition passes, NJSP electronically sends it to the NJOAG and Prosecutor’s Offices.
  • Judges authorize the final expungement order and send the decision to the New Jersey eCourt system.
  • The final decision returns to the NJSP, NJOAG, and Prosecutor’s Offices to expunge the information in all relevant New Jersey databases.
Overall, automating the expungement process has streamlined every part of the workflow resulting in remarkably quicker assessments. Gerald Dezenzo, our experienced account manager, explains, “It’s a huge change and a significant improvement. All the petition information comes through the interface, through the service, and into the NJSP application in a clean and precise manner. This cuts down the NJSP’s review time considerably.” As new legislation evolves, the robust expungement system continues to adapt to the changes in criminal justice reform.

Aligning to Serve the Public

The success of the New Jersey Expungement Project exemplifies effective collaboration and alignment among different government agencies working towards a common objective. The implementation of this new expungement system has significantly expedited the process of record expungement under the new laws, which otherwise may have taken over a decade to complete manually. As Joshua Ottenberg highlights, “CSI brings a unique set of skills to the table when we approach a complex project like this because our account management staff and leadership is drawn almost exclusively from the ranks of government agencies. We have a background and a basis of knowledge that plays into the success of this project. Our team is composed of highly experienced engineers, who transformed the project’s vision into reality, and former public servants, who know all too well what happens when the system fails its citizens. This fuels our unwavering dedication to streamlining government operations to improve the quality of life for all.” Ottenberg concludes, “The benefits of the expungement system will be felt for years to come by the general public, who will no longer have to worry about a minor criminal incident that happened in their life years ago.” CSI looks forward to a long-lasting partnership with the NJOAG, NJSP, NJAOC, and Prosecutor’s Offices as we work toward a promising future in overall criminal justice reform.

title: CSI Technology Group is the First Vendor to Complete New Hampshire SFTP NFIRS Integration
shareTitle: CSI Technology Group is the First Vendor to Complete New Hampshire SFTP NFIRS Integration
brief: CSI Technology Group is the first CAD/RMS vendor to complete the New Hampshire Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) integration for National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS) reporting.
body:
CSI Technology Group is the first CAD/RMS vendor to complete the New Hampshire Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) integration for National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS) reporting. The submission of NFIRS has evolved over the years and currently the NHFMO receives fire service data files via e-mail attachments. This method works well, but the increase in fraudulent access to e-mail accounts may create concern about the safety and security of this method. As a result, the state decided that all New Hampshire Fire Departments will need to submit their reporting through the State of New Hampshire Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) only; e-mails will not be accepted. With this change, New Hampshire Fire Departments need an easy and secure pathway to submit NFIRS reports.

Prior to the transition, New Hampshire Fire Departments would write NFIRS reports in a third-party program, download the completed report, manually log into the SFTP page, and upload and send the file. CSI recognized the need to adapt to changing policies so the implementation of the New Hampshire SFTP with NFIRS reporting has streamlined the workflow efficiency for report writing and submission. As Deputy Robert Farley shares, “The NHFMO (NH State Fire Marshal's Office) started to migrate towards the secure FTP data file transfer method several years ago in order to improve the security of the fire service data being transmitted to our office. While not specifically covered under HIPAA, the NHFMO has always treated NFIRS data with a similar level of security as it does contain some personally identifiable information (PII). We believe the data belongs to the local fire department, and we are just shepherds of that data on its way to the national database.”

CSI’s New Hampshire SFTP NFIRS integration will help simplify the data submission process for all New Hampshire Fire Departments using the InfoShare Fire/EMS RMS application. Under this change, New Hampshire Fire Departments can now write and submit the entire NFIRS report through InfoShare FireRMS. This keeps the file sharing secure since NFIRS reports are automatically pushed to the NHFMO without having to separately download and re-upload the reports from a device.

CSI’s integration of the NHSFTP and NFIRS has eased the reporting process for our department. The process is very intuitive and functional. With two clicks of a mouse, your monthly NFIRS report list is packaged and sent to the State via secure file transfer protocol. Additionally, you are provided the option to view a comprehensive monthly report list with links to the NFIRS reports prior to sending if the need arises. The CSI team takes customer input very seriously and works diligently to create a product that meets the needs of our department.

Craig Chabot
Deputy Chief
City of Dover Fire and Rescue
Since the state’s decision to switch to the SFTP method only, our CSI clients have experienced the convenience and efficiency of our SFTP NFIRS integration. CSI Technology Group remains committed to the relationship we have with the NHFIRS program and the New Hampshire Division of Fire Safety. We will continue to work together to ensure that all our Fire/EMS RMS clients have the most up-to-date solutions available to them.

title: New Taipei City Fire Department Launches the InfoShare<sup>®</sup> Intelligent Fire Service Platform to Protect and Serve Its Citizens
shareTitle: New Taipei City Fire Department Launches the InfoShare® Intelligent Fire Service Platform to Protect and Serve Its Citizens
brief: Since 2021, CSI Technology Group's Taiwan Division has embarked on a collaborative journey with the New Taipei City Fire Department (NTFD) through the Global Innovation Partnership Initiatives Program of the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs.
body:
Since 2021, CSI Technology Group's Taiwan Division has embarked on a collaborative journey with the New Taipei City Fire Department (NTFD) through the Global Innovation Partnership Initiatives Program of the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs. The partnership leveraged CSI Technology Group's advanced technology and fire product development experience in the United States, along with the expertise of the NTFD. This collaboration led to the groundbreaking creation of the Intelligent Fire Service Platform (IFS), which stands as Taiwan's pioneer in cloud-based information management for fire service operations and business processes. To highlight these achievements, the NTFD featured this milestone in the April 2023 issue of the Fire Safety Monthly Magazine published by the Taiwan National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior.

The jurisdiction of the NTFD covers the area with the highest population, the most fire and rescue incidents, the largest geographical expanse, and the most complex range of disaster types (including typhoons, earthquakes, active volcanoes, and high density population structures) in Taiwan. Therefore, it is also the fire department with the most firefighters in the country. However, in the past, the data from all the branches of the NTFD was stored in disparate systems or even in paper logbooks, posing challenges to effectively analyzing and utilizing the information.

The Intelligent Fire Service Platform (IFS) interconnects these data through a cloud-based platform. By establishing a database and digitizing and structuring the data in a standardized electronic format instead of in paper logbooks, the NTFD can conduct regional analyses of fire incidents. This allows for detailed risk analysis for resource allocation and work hour statistical analysis for manpower resources of all the branches. This achieves the objectives of digitizing, automating, mobilizing, and personalizing fire service operations and business processes. Moreover, it lays the foundation for future big data analysis and artificial intelligence applications for efficiency when planning for and responding to a wide variety of natural and man-made disasters.

The IFS was officially launched in June 2022, and over 2,000 users actively use the platform. At the same time, the NTFD Command and Control Elements can also easily monitor the status of the fire service operations and business processes of all branches through the IFS. Nowadays, the IFS has become a crucial real-time cornerstone of the operations of the fire department.

The homepage layout of IFS

Currently, CSI Technology Group's Taiwan Division continues to invest in research and development to enhance the digitalization of fire service operations, business processes, and fire records management. The Intelligent Fire Service - Mobile Virtual Shift (IFS-MVS) is the latest application developed by CSI Technology Group's Taiwan Division. It is based on the technology framework of the IFS and leverages the patented low-code development platform, InfoShare® Engine. When a fire incident occurs, the IFS-MVS can integrate with the dispatch system, allowing on-duty firefighters to receive real-time incident information from the dispatch center on their mobile devices. Additionally, the hardware equipment at the fire station, including sirens, broadcasting systems, lights, and garage doors will also activate automatically.

The Intelligent Fire Service - Mobile Virtual Shift (IFS-MVS) was successfully implemented in the Linkou and Banqiao branches of the NTFD in 2022. Based on statistical analysis, the implementation of the IFS-MVS has resulted in a decrease in the average turnout time of the two branches from 80 seconds to 60 seconds. This represents a 1.3-fold improvement in response efficiency. Furthermore, the watchkeepers at the Command desk, who previously had to manually activate the hardware equipment upon receiving fire incident notifications from the dispatch center, can now don their gear 86 seconds faster, achieving synchronized readiness. The NTFD plans to gradually implement the IFS-MVS into all of their branches, divisions, and districts in the near future.

The app layout of IFS-MVS

The layout of the environmental control management function of IFS-MVS

The Intelligent Fire Service Platform (IFS) is designed by firefighters for firefighters from a product perspective, providing an integrated and comprehensive solution for the management of fire service operations and business processes. In the future, this comprehensive solution can not only be applied to other fire departments in Taiwan, but also exported to the United States markets through CSI Technology Group's sales channels. CSI Technology Group's Taiwan Division aims to continue enhancing the international visibility of Taiwan's research and development capabilities and expertise. Firefighting is a dangerous job no matter where in the world you are. The NTFD has one of the highest and most diverse call volumes in the world, and much can be gleaned from their expertise. As with all CSI clients across the globe, we are proud to call the NTFD our partners.

title: CSI Achieves NEMSIS Compliance and ePCR Certification: What It Means for Our Clients

The National Emergency Medical Services Information System (NEMSIS) is the national gold standard for EMS data collection, reporting, and interoperability for emergency 911 call information. Managed by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA)’s Office of EMS, it ensures that EMS providers and software platforms speak a common language to promote data quality, patient safety, and operational consistency across the country.

Only NEMSIS-compliant software is allowed to access and contribute to the national EMS repository. Being NEMSIS-compliant means that our InfoShare® EMS solution meets rigorous federal standards, delivering accurate, validated, and transportable patient care data that can be relied upon in critical, life-saving moments. This also enables cross-agency communication, advanced analytics, and regulatory alignment.

What Is ePCR Certification?

An Electronic Patient Care Reporting (ePCR) system is the digital backbone of EMS documentation. It ensures that every patient interaction, from the first point of contact to handoff at the hospital, is recorded accurately, securely, and in real time.

Our ePCR-certified platform is designed to:
  • Fully comply with both state-specific and national reporting requirements.
  • Protect patient data with HIPAA-compliant security protocols.
  • Support seamless data sharing with hospitals, billing systems, and public health agencies.
By achieving ePCR certification, we offer our clients a platform that enhances clinical decision-making, regulatory readiness, and administrative efficiency to help them stay ahead in a fast-evolving healthcare landscape.

title: Delaware County DA’s Office Streamlines Case Management with InfoShare<sup>®</sup> Local Police Agency RMS and AOPC Interface
shareTitle: Delaware County DA’s Office Streamlines Case Management with InfoShare® Local Police Agency RMS and AOPC Interface
brief: In the spring of 2024, the Delaware County District Attorney’s Office in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania began a critical modernization project with CSI Technology Group to build a direct, automated interface between its InfoShare® eProsecution module, the local police InfoShare® RMS, and the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts (AOPC).
body:
In the spring of 2024, the Delaware County District Attorney’s Office in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania began a critical modernization project with CSI Technology Group to build a direct, automated interface between its InfoShare® eProsecution module, the local police InfoShare® RMS, and the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts (AOPC).

With over 80 users across the DA’s office, the shift to a bi-directional electronic interface has transformed how prosecutors receive and manage cases. What once required phone calls, manual data entry, and clerical follow-up is now a seamless digital process that is reliable, accurate, and automatic.

Discovery and Documents: From Manual Processes to Automated Workflows

Previously, staff had to call local police departments to request case files, wait for court docket updates, and manually enter information into internal systems. This process caused delays, introduced possible errors, and consumed valuable staff time.

Today, with InfoShare® and the AOPC interface:
  • Bi-directional automation ensures cases flow seamlessly between the DA’s office and the courts.
  • District court cases and common pleas are pushed electronically into InfoShare® eProsecution module, eliminating the need for manual requests.
  • Case requests can still be initiated by the DA if a file is not automatically pushed over.
  • Currently, 23 Police RMS case documents and counting are electronically sent directly to the DA, replacing the need for follow-up phone calls to local police departments.
  • Updates every 30 minutes automatically pull in new cases and criminal docket changes from the AOPC, ensuring DA staff always work with the most current information.
  • Auto-populated case data reduces clerical work and improves data accuracy.
By the end of the year, the DA’s office will implement the eDiscovery Portal:
  • Discovery documents will be electronically transferred to the Public Defender’s Office and private defense attorneys through a cloud-based portal.
  • Defense attorneys can make a request for discovery directly to the District Attorney’s Office and download all relevant documents sent for their cases.

Benefits for Prosecutors and Staff

The results of the new interface are already evident:
  • Efficiency: Prosecutors gain immediate access to new cases and docket updates without waiting on manual workflows.
  • Accuracy: Automated data transfer minimizes clerical errors, ensuring case information is reliable and complete.
  • Time savings: Staff no longer spend hours tracking cases or calling local police departments for records.
  • Consistency: Every 30 minutes, InfoShare® eProsecution module updates the DA’s office with the latest court and police case activity, ensuring continuity.
  • Scalability: With over 80 users leveraging the platform, the system supports both high-volume case intake and day-to-day prosecutorial work.

A Smarter, Connected Justice System

The Delaware County District Attorney’s Office is now positioned at the forefront of digital transformation in Pennsylvania’s justice system. By moving to a fully electronic and automated interface with the InfoShare® RMS and the AOPC, the county has eliminated inefficiencies and created a foundation for long-term operational continuity.

“Our goal is to remove the friction that slows down justice,” said James Parent, Deputy Director of the County and State Agency Division at CSI Technology Group. “This initiative shows how smart technology can aid and strengthen our courts. By automating the exchange of cases and court data, Delaware County’s prosecutors now have a system that works for them without increasing their workload.”

The impact is clear: prosecutors can spend less time chasing paperwork and more time pursuing justice. Delaware County has redefined what it means to work smarter, faster, and more collaboratively in today’s prosecutorial environment.

title: New Jersey’s Affordable Housing Reform: Powered by Low-Code Innovation for Stronger Communities

body:

New Jersey is restructuring how affordable housing is managed statewide to strengthen affordable housing access and streamline compliance across all 565 municipalities. With the enactment of Public Law 2024, c.2, the state dissolved the Council on Affordable Housing (COAH) and transferred oversight to the Department of Community Affairs (DCA). Built on CSI’s configurable low-code platform, this application enables the DCA to swiftly adapt to evolving legal and operational changes without costly redevelopment. The purpose-built software aligns directly with the new statute and includes features like:
  • Real-time oversight and submission of trust fund data, compliance plans, and development fee reports
  • Compliance management
  • Built-in document management
  • Integrated validation rules for data accuracy and audit readiness
  • Transparent and scalable administration
A key component of this initiative is its seamless integration with the myNewJersey Portal, New Jersey’s official digital gateway for government services. Municipalities across the state will now access all affordable housing functions through this centralized, secure platform. The integration enhances the user experience and safeguards sensitive data while streamlining operations. Key features of the portal include:
  • Secure, role-based access for municipal staff, DCA administrators, and housing stakeholders
  • Streamlined user experience within the familiar myNewJersey interface
  • State-standard security, including multi-factor authentication and encrypted communication

Legacy Data to Modern Utility

Keith Henderson, Director of Local Planning Services at the Department of Community Affairs, shares how “within weeks of the legislation’s passage, [CSI] had a solution in place and a dedicated team to support our transition. Migrating decades of legacy COAH data into the new Affordable Housing Monitoring System (AHMS) using the InfoShare® platform not only ensured historical continuity but also reduced municipal resource expenditures and strengthened the State’s ability to monitor progress over time. Their readiness and deep understanding of government operations made them an invaluable partner throughout this process.”

The new platform enables municipalities to manage tasks and responsibilities through guided workflows and automatically flags trust fund overspending risks. With every data submission, the system strengthens interagency communication and streamlines reporting across local and state levels.

“This project is a clear example of how low-code platforms and experienced data conversions can transform public policy into working, maintainable systems” said John Porter, Director of the County and State Products at CSI Technology Group. “It reflects our commitment to using technology that evolves alongside the law to better serve communities, with accountability and responsiveness built in from day one.”

Technology as a Long-Term Public Asset

In an age where digital infrastructure enhances public service capacity, New Jersey’s partnership with CSI Technology Group establishes a new operational standard. By combining policy reform with a secure, cloud-based low-code solution, the state is advancing affordable housing delivery with speed, transparency, and precision. This is more than a system upgrade. It is a strategic investment in government technology that strengthens municipal performance, builds public trust, and delivers lasting outcomes for communities across the state.
